content:
请阅读下面短文，在所给的每个空格中填入一个形式正确、意义相符的单词，并将答案写在答题卡对应题目的答题位置上。

weak save dangerous lady and with tell but snake happy

Do you know the story of Madame White Snake (白蛇传)? It is a very famous Chinese story. It [[41]] a love story between White Snake and Xu xian.

Once upon a time there were two snakes—White Snake and Green Snake. They had magic and could turn themselves into two beautiful young [[42]]. At the West Lake of Hangzhou, they met a man called Xuxian. White Snake quickly fell in love [[43]]. They got married soon and lived together [[44]] him.

The Dragon Boat Festival came. On that day, people usually drank realgar wine (雄黄酒). But it was [[45]] for White Snake to drink this kind of wine. If she drank the wine, she would turn into the[[46]] again. However, Xuxian didn't know anything about it. So he asked his wife to drink realgar wine together. Soon White snake felt tired [[47]] weak. She fell asleep on the bed. When Xuxian went into the room, he could not find [[48]] wife. He only saw a huge (巨大的) white snake. He was so scared [[49]] got seriously ill.

In order to [[50]] her husband , White Snake went to steal (偷) the magical medicine. In the end, the god got moved because of her true love, so he saved Xuxian. What a moving love story!
explanation:
句意：它讲述了白蛇和许仙之间的爱情故事。按句意，应该是“讲述/是”一个爱情故事，主语It为第三人称单数，描述一般事实，选“tell”，但要变成第三人称单数形式“tells”。

句意：她们有法力，可以把自己变成两个美丽的年轻女士。按句意，应该是“女士/女子”，指白蛇和青蛇变成的人类形象，选“lady”，但要变成复数形式“ladies”。

句意：白蛇很快就与他相爱了。按句意，应该是“与”他相爱，“fall in love with”是固定短语，意为“与……相爱”，后面要接宾语“him”，表示与许仙相爱，所以填with。

句意：她们很快就结婚了，并且快乐地生活在一起。按句意，应该是“快乐地”生活在一起，选happy，修饰动词“lived”要用副词形式，所以变成副词形式“happily”。

句意：但是喝这种酒对白蛇来说是危险的。因为喝了会现出原形，空格处应该是表示“危险的”的形容词，选“danger”，要变成形容词形式“dangerous”。

句意：如果她喝了酒，就会再次变成蛇。按句意，应该是“蛇”，指变回蛇的原形，选snake，主语“she”是单数，用单数形式“snake”即可。

句意：很快白蛇感到疲劳和虚弱。按句意连接两个并列的形容词“tired”和“weak”，应该是“和”，所以填and。

句意：当许仙走进房间时，他找不到他的妻子了。按句意，应该是“他的”妻子，修饰名词“wife”，所以选“he”，但要变成形容词性物主代词形式“his”。

句意：他非常害怕，而且病得很重。按句意，空格处应该表示两个动作的并列，用“and”。

句意：为了拯救她的丈夫，白蛇去偷仙草。按句意，应该是“拯救”她的丈夫，作动词用，选save，“in order to do sth.”意为“为了做某事”，填动词原形“save”即可。

A

Accidents may happen in our daily life. Learning first aid skills can help us deal with them quickly and properly. Here is some useful advice when someone is in an emergency.

Getting a burn

* Run cool water over the burn for 10 to 20 minutes first.

* Take off any clothing near the burn.

* Cover the burn with a clean bandage or cloth.

Having a [[_]]

* Try to keep the person cool and make sure they drink lots of water.

* Give the person medicine to lower the temperature.

Choking

* If the person can cough, talk or breathe, don’t do anything-let them try to get the object out by themselves.

* If the person can’t cough, talk or breathe, stand behind them and lean them forward. Hit their back firmly five times. If the object remains, push on their stomach five times.

* Keep doing five back hits and five stomach pushes one after the other. Do not stop until the object comes out.

Bleeding heavily

* Press on the wound with a clean cloth or bandage until the bleeding stops. Remember not to clean the wound first.

* If the bleeding doesn’t stop, tie a bandage around the area above the wound.

* Keep the wound raised if possible.
content: According to the text, what should you do first if someone gets a burn?
options: Cover the burn with a bandage.
Take off clothing near the burn.
Run cool water over the burn.
Put some medicine onto the burn.
explanation: 根据文中“Getting a burn”部分的“Run cool water over the burn for 10 to 20 minutes first.”可知，有人被烧伤时，首先要用冷水冲洗伤口。

subject: english
material:
Kevin was a shy teenager who had trouble making friends. He felt lonely most of the time and often sat alone during lunch. Although he wanted to connect with others, he didn’t know how to start a conversation.

One day, a new student named Leo joined Kevin’s class. During lunch, Leo sat down next to Kevin and said, “Hi, I’m Leo. Is this seat taken?” Kevin shook his head nervously. “My name is Kevin,” he said quietly.

The next day, Leo invited Kevin to play basketball with him and some other classmates. Kevin was surprised but agreed. At first, he was clumsy and missed most of his shots. But Leo encouraged him and said, “Don’t worry. Practice makes perfect.”

Weeks passed, and Kevin grew more confident. He started to talk more and even made a few new friends. He realized that a small act of kindness could change everything.

subject: english
material:
Among all the natural wonders in the world, Lake Baikal in Russia always impresses me the most. It is not just a lake, but a miracle created by nature, full of unique beauty and secrets.

Lake Baikal is one of the oldest lakes on Earth, with a history of about 25 million years. It is also the deepest freshwater lake in the world, reaching a depth of 1,637 meters. The lake lies in the shape of a crescent moon, and its water is so clear that you can see small fish swimming freely under the surface. In summer, the lake looks like a huge blue mirror, reflecting the green mountains around it. In winter, the lake freezes, and the ice becomes as thick as 60 centimeters, creating a world of white and blue.

What makes Lake Baikal really special is its rich ecosystem. It is home to over 1,700 species of plants and animals, and two-thirds of them can’t be found anywhere else in the world. For example, the Baikal seal is a unique animal that only lives here. The lake also provides clean water for millions of people nearby and helps regulate the local climate.

People from all over the world come to visit Lake Baikal every year. They enjoy the beautiful scenery, take a boat trip on the lake, or walk along the shore. But more importantly, they come to feel the power of nature. Standing by the lake, you will realize how small humans are compared to nature.

Lake Baikal is a precious gift from nature. It is our duty to protect it. We should stop polluting the water and avoid damaging the ecosystem. Only in this way can we keep this natural wonder beautiful for future generations.
content: Where is Lake Baikal located?
explanation: 第一段第一句“Lake Baikal in Russia always impresses me the most.”，贝加尔湖在“俄罗斯”。

material:

Yellow Crane Tower, on the south bank (河岸) of the Yangtze River, is a landmark of Wuhan City. [[31]]

Throughout history, Yellow Crane Tower has gone through many ups and downs. [[32]] The existing (现存的) building was rebuilt in 1985 according to the style (风格) of the Qing Dynasty (朝代).

Yellow Crane Tower, together with Yueyang Tower in Hunan and Tengwang Pavilion in Jiangxi, is known as one of the “Three Great Towers of Jiangnan”. [[33]]

The tower is famous because of the poem Yellow Crane Tower. [[34]] The poem describes the amazing scenery seen from the tower and the feeling of parting (离别). It makes the building a symbol of Chinese literature and culture.

Yellow Crane Tower has 5 floors and is about 51.4 metres high. [[35]] Inside the tower, there are many ancient paintings, calligraphy works and cultural relics (古迹). They show the long history of this place.
options: It has been rebuilt (被重修) many times.
At first, it was a place for parties and fun.
It’s also a symbol of the ancient Chu civilization.
It was written by the poet Cui Hao in the Tang Dynasty.
People also praise it as “China’s No.1 Poetry Tower”.
Tourists can climb up to the top and enjoy the scenery of the Yangtze River and Wuhan City. Every year, thousands of tourists come here to enjoy its beauty and recall the wonderful poem.
explanation: 第一段开篇点明黄鹤楼是武汉地标，空1需要补充它的文化象征意义。选项C“It’s also a symbol of the ancient Chu civilization.”（它也是古代楚文化的象征）承接了“地标”的介绍，进一步升华其文化价值，逻辑连贯。

subject: english
content:
阅读短文，从方框中选出恰当的单词并用其适当形式填空，使短文通顺，意义完整。每空仅填一词，每词仅用一次。

climber clear quick we though

enter harm wonder throw change

I have enjoyed outdoor (户外的) activities for many years. Several days ago, I saw the natural [[36]] of Mount Tai with my own eyes. Many [[37]] told us that we’d better bring warm clothes, because the weather was greatly [[38]]. They advised us not to [[39]] the dangerous areas without a guide. The mountain [[40]] showed different challenges at every stage. Some tourists [[41]] rubbish on purpose. This kind of action really did [[42]] to the environment. As we climbed higher, our steps became much [[43]] in order to reach the mountain top before sunset (日落). We all felt tired, but we encouraged [[44]] to keep going.

[[45]] my legs were sore the next day, I felt proud of what we achieved together.
answer: (1) wonder##wonders；(2) climbers；(3) changeable；(4) enter；(5) clearly；(6) threw；(7) harm；(8) quicker；(9) ourselves；(10) Though
explanation:
句意：几天前，我亲眼看到了泰山的自然奇观。“the natural [[_]] of Mount Tai”表示“泰山的自然奇观”，需选wonder“奇观”，为可数名词，若将泰山视为一整个自然奇观，强调整体概念，用单数形式wonder；若侧重泰山内部多处景致、奇观，强调多样景观，用复数wonders。

句意：许多登山者告诉我们最好带上暖和的衣服。“Many [[_]] told us”中，需选名词climber，意为“登山者”，many后需用复数形式climbers。

句意：因为天气变化很大。“the weather was greatly [[_]]”表示“天气变化很大”，was后需用形容词作表语。需选change“变化”，其形容词形式为changeable，意为“易变的，变化大的”。

句意：他们建议我们不要在没有向导的情况下进入危险区域。“not to [[_]] the dangerous areas”中，advise sb. not to do sth.需用动词原形。需选enter“进入”，为动词原形。

句意：这座山清晰地展现了每个阶段的不同挑战。“The mountain [[_]] showed different challenges”表示“这座山清晰地展现了不同挑战”，需用副词修饰动词showed。需选clear“清楚的”，其副词形式为clearly，意为“清楚地”。

句意：一些游客故意扔垃圾。“Some tourists [[_]] rubbish on purpose”中，描述过去发生的事情需用一般过去时。需选throw“扔”，其过去式为threw。

句意：这种行为确实对环境造成了伤害。“did [[_]] to the environment”中，do harm to为固定短语，意为“对……造成伤害”，需选harm“伤害”，为不可数名词。

If you get angry many times in a day, it is time for you to think about how to deal with it. Here are some of my suggestions.

When you are angry, try to tell yourself through another voice that you are angry and that it is not a bad thing. It just shows that you have different ideas. Accept that many things are not 100% right or wrong, our communication with others, the final purpose is not to decide who is right and who is wrong, but to look for something in common.

If you still feel strong anger, try taking a deep breath and let anger out of your body along with the breath. Don’t say angry words when you are very angry, for you will regret saying them when you cool down.

Discussing with a third party is helpful. It is hard for the two parties in anger to understand each other. But the idea of an outsider can help both parties to get mutual (相互的) understanding.

Anger is just one of the many emotions that make us human, and to well manage it adds to our ability to truly understand the world.

content:
As a senior high school freshman，I’ve been trying to adapt to the new learning environment.Since the term began，my classmates and I [[1]](build) a close friendship by supporting each other.Last week，our class held a debate competition，which [[2]](prove) to be a great success.

To prepare for it，we spent several evenings [[3]](discuss) topics and collecting materials.Our teacher advised us [[4]](express) our opinions clearly and logically.During the competition，everyone spoke [[5]](confident)，and the judges praised us for our excellent performance.

One of the topics was about the importance of after-class activities.Some students argued that participating in sports or clubs helps develop [[6]](person) skills.I shared my experience of joining the English club,[[7]] I’d made progress in spoken English.

[[8]] competition also taught us the value of teamwork.Without the efforts of every member，we couldn’t have achieved such good results.Now，we often stay after class to practice debating，and we believe that consistent practice is the key [[9]] improving our abilities.

Our teacher often tells us that success comes from hard work and perseverance.We should cherish the opportunities we have at school and make the most of [[10]](we) time.In the future，I hope we can take part in more such meaningful activities to enrich our school life.
explanation:
考查动词时态和主谓一致。根据Since the term began可知，句子应用现在完成时，主语是my classmates and I，是复数，助动词用have。故填have built。

考查动词时态。根据Last week可知，句子描述的是过去的事情，应用一般过去时，prove的过去式是proved。故填proved。

考查非谓语动词。spend time (in) doing sth意为“花费时间做某事”，空处应用动名词作宾语。故填discussing。

考查非谓语动词。advise sb to do sth意为“建议某人做某事”，空处应用动词不定式作宾语补足语。故填to express。

考查副词。空处修饰动词spoke，应用副词作状语。故填confidently。

考查形容词。空处修饰名词skills，应用形容词作定语。故填personal。

考查定语从句。空处引导非限制性定语从句，修饰先行词the English club，先行词在从句中作地点状语，应用关系副词where引导从句。故填where。

考查冠词。此处特指上文提到的a debate competition，应用定冠词the；位于句首，首字母应大写。故填The。

考查介词。the key to...意为“……的关键”，是固定搭配，所以空处应用介词to。故填to。

考查代词。空处修饰名词time，应用形容词性物主代词作定语。故填our。

subject: english
material:
I was 13 years old.My family moved from North Florida to Southern California a year before.Everything around me was new and strange，and I missed my old friends deeply.I was angry and stubborn(固执的) because I couldn’t get used to this big change.Like many teenagers，I tried to stay away from things that didn’t fit my idea of the world.I thought I was “good without needing help” and refused any love from others.

One night，after a really hard day，I ran into my room，closed the door and lay on the bed.My hands touched an envelope(信封) under my pillow.I took it out.On the envelope，it said，“To read when you’re alone.” I opened it.It was from Mom: “Mike，I know life is hard now，you’re upset(心烦意乱的)，and we don’t do everything right.But I love you completely，and nothing you do or say will change that.I am here for you，and I love you forever.Love，Mom.” This was the first of many such letters.Each one arrived quietly，always at a moment when I needed it most.

Now I travel around the world to help people.In Florida，a woman told me she had trouble with her son.I told her about my mom’s endless love and the “To read when you’re alone” letters.Weeks later，she sent me a card saying she wrote her first letter for her son，which greatly improved their relationship.Now，when life is hard，I remember those letters.They reminded me I was loved even with my mistakes.Unconditional love changed my life.
content: Why was the writer angry and stubborn?
options: He didn’t like his new school.
He didn’t get along well with his parents.
He wanted to escape from his parents’ control.
He struggled to fit in with his new environment.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据第一段的“Everything around me was new and strange...I was angry and stubborn(固执的) because I couldn’t get used to this big change.”可知，作者生气且固执是因为他努力想要适应新的环境却未能成功。故选D。

material:
Practicing Self Care

No matter how far along you are in your studies，doing well in school can be challenging.You can perform at your best by developing healthy study habits and staying organized. [[1]]

Get good-quality sleep.

[[2]] You can practice good sleep by going to bed early enough each night，turning off bright screens at least half an hour before bed，and keeping your room quiet，dark，and comfortable.To help you sleep better，try to go to bed and wake up at the same time every day.

Do stress-relieving(释放压力的) activities.

Take time to relax and do things you enjoy.You’ll do much better in school if you aren’t anxious all the time. [[3]] These activities can be relaxing and enriching，and they’re also a good way for you to get to know your teachers and fellow students.

Reward yourself.

When you get something done，take the time to celebrate！For example，after an hour of studying，you might reward yourself with a favorite snack.Or，if you do well on a big test，you could celebrate by going out for pizza with your friends. [[4]]

[[5]]

If the stress of school is getting to you，sometimes just talking to a friend about how you’re feeling can help you feel better.Also，don’t be afraid to ask for practical support.You could say，“Mom，I’m really stressing about this test.Can you take a few minutes and quiz me with some questions from the review sheet？”
options: Try joining a school sports team or reading club.
You can also feel your best by taking care of yourself.
You won’t do well in school if you’re too tired to focus.

material:

No matter how far along you are in your studies，doing well in school can be challenging.You can perform at your best by developing healthy study habits and staying organized. [[1]]

Get good-quality sleep.

[[2]] You can practice good sleep by going to bed early enough each night，turning off bright screens at least half an hour before bed，and keeping your room quiet，dark，and comfortable.To help you sleep better，try to go to bed and wake up at the same time every day.

Do stress-relieving(释放压力的) activities.

Take time to relax and do things you enjoy.You’ll do much better in school if you aren’t anxious all the time. [[3]] These activities can be relaxing and enriching，and they’re also a good way for you to get to know your teachers and fellow students.

When you get something done，take the time to celebrate！For example，after an hour of studying，you might reward yourself with a favorite snack.Or，if you do well on a big test，you could celebrate by going out for pizza with your friends. [[4]]

[[5]]

content: Jiangmen is famous [[_]] its Kaiping Diaolou and Xinhui Chenpi.

subject: english
content:
—Which do you like to drink, coke or coffee?

—[[_]]. I prefer to drink green tea!
explanation:
句意：——你喜欢喝哪种饮料，可乐还是咖啡？——都不喜欢。我更喜欢喝绿茶！

Either两者之一；Neither两者都不；Both两者都；None三者或三者以上都不。根据“I prefer to drink green tea!”可知，说话人既不喜欢可乐也不喜欢咖啡，表示两者都不喜欢。

subject: english
content: What a [[_]] story! We are all [[_]] with it.
explanation:
句意：一个多么无聊的故事啊！我们都对它感到无聊。

boring令人无聊的，常修饰事或物；bored感到无聊的，常修饰人。第一空后的名词story“故事”，指物，应用boring修饰，排除选项A和D；第二空主语是We“我们”，指人，表示人的感受，应用bored修饰，排除选项B。

subject: english
content:
anything 任何东西；nothing 没有什么；everything 一切；something 某事，某物。通常疑问句中用anything，但在表示建议、请求或希望得到对方肯定回答的疑问句中，常用something。根据答语“Yes”可知此处表示建议并希望得到肯定回答，something符合该语境逻辑，其他选项均不符合，应选something。

6. Jack, please [[_]] carefully to the teacher!
explanation:

listens听（listen的第三人称单数形式）；listening听（listen的现在分词形式）；listen听（动词原形）；listened听（listen的过去式形式）。根据“Jack, please...carefully to the teacher!”可知，该句为祈使句，please后接动词原形。

content: The man looks [[_]] and he looks [[_]] at me.

happy高兴的，是形容词；happily高兴地，是副词。第一空，looks“看起来”是系动词，其后接形容词作表语，happy是形容词，排除选项C和D；第二空，looks at“看”是动词短语，副词修饰动词，happily是副词，排除选项A。

content: I don’t like bread, rice [[_]] porridge, I like meat.
explanation:
句意：我不喜欢面包、米饭或粥，我喜欢肉。

and和；but但是；so所以；or或者。根据句中“I don’t like”可知是否定句，在否定句中表示并列关系通常用or而不用and。

subject: english
content: Guangzhou is one of [[_]] cities in China.
explanation:
句意：广州是中国最大的城市之一。

big大的，形容词原形；bigger更大的，形容词比较级；the biggest最大的，形容词最高级。根据固定句型“one of the + 形容词最高级 + 名词复数”，表示“最……之一”，最高级前需加定冠词the。因此，应填the biggest。

subject: english
content: [[_]] you listen in class, [[_]] you will learn.

句子是固定结构“the+比较级，the+比较级”结构，意为“越……，越……”，careful仔细的，是形容词；carefully仔细地，是副词；much许多，是原级；more是much的比较级，第一空，修饰动词listen“听”，用副词，用副词carefully的比较级more carefully；排除选项A和D；第二空，应用much的比较级more，排除选项C。

More and more people in the United States are becoming couch potatoes. They are on their couches watching something. They are also often eating snacks like potato chips. This is the reason why these people are called couch potatoes.

Being a couch potato can have other health risks besides being fat. The reason is that more and more people are sitting in front of a television screen, and do not exercise at all. This is one reason why heart disease is a leading cause of death in the country. Another problem is the weakness in muscles (肌肉). It influences people’s mental (心理) health, too. Sitting inside in front of a screen usually means a person is spending less time with friends and loved ones. This can also lead to other problems such as loneliness.

Being a couch potato is not just for adults. [[_]]. This is why there are programs like Let’s Move, encouraging kids to take more part in physical activities.

subject: english
content:
配对阅读。左栏是五个人的兴趣爱好的介绍，右栏是六个城市的介绍。请为每个人匹配对应的城市。选项中有两项为多余项。

[[31]] David likes the sea and sunshine. He wants to spend his holiday on the beach.

[[32]] Ben is interested in technology. He enjoys modern life and would like to go shopping.

[[33]] Emma is an art fan and wants to visit famous museums. She dreams of visiting a romantic city.

[[34]] Amy loves history very much. She wants to learn about ancient cultures and see old buildings.

[[35]] Cathy is tired of her busy school life. She hopes to find a quiet place with beautiful natural scenery.

A. Paris is famous for its art, museums and beautiful buildings. You can visit the Louvre and enjoy the city of romance.

B. Sydney is a great place for people who love the sea. You can enjoy the sunshine, beaches and the famous Opera House.

C. Tokyo is a modern city with advanced technology. You can also enjoy delicious food and exciting shopping there.

D. Cairo is a wonderful place to learn history. You can visit the pyramids and learn about ancient Egypt.

E. New York is a busy city with many tall buildings. You can watch shows, go shopping and enjoy city life.

F. Zurich is quiet and clean, with beautiful lakes and mountains. It is a good place to relax and enjoy nature.
explanation:
David喜欢大海和阳光，想去海滩度假。根据选项 B “Sydney is a great place for people who love the sea. You can enjoy the sunshine, beaches and the famous Opera House.（悉尼是热爱大海的人的好去处。你可以享受阳光、海滩和著名的歌剧院。）”可推知悉尼符合大卫的需求。故填B。

Ben对科技感兴趣，喜欢现代生活和购物。根据选项 C “Tokyo is a modern city with advanced technology. You can also enjoy delicious food and exciting shopping there.（东京是一个拥有先进技术的现代化城市。你也可以在那里享受美食和令人兴奋的购物。）”可推知东京符合本的需求。故填 C。

Emma 是艺术迷，想参观著名博物馆，梦想去浪漫城市。根据选项 A “Paris is famous for its art, museums and beautiful buildings. You can visit the Louvre and enjoy the city of romance.（巴黎以其艺术、博物馆和美丽的建筑而闻名。你可以参观卢浮宫，享受浪漫之城。）”可推知巴黎符合艾玛的需求。故填A。

Amy 非常热爱历史，想了解古代文化和看老建筑。根据选项 D “Cairo is a wonderful place to learn history. You can visit the pyramids and learn about ancient Egypt.（开罗是学习历史的好地方。你可以参观金字塔，了解古埃及。）”可推知开罗符合艾米的需求。故填D。

Cathy厌倦了忙碌的学校生活，希望找一个安静、风景优美的地方。根据选项 F “Zurich is quiet and clean, with beautiful lakes and mountains. It is a good place to relax and enjoy nature.（苏黎世安静干净，拥有美丽的湖泊和山脉。这是一个放松和享受自然的好地方。）”可推知苏黎世符合凯西的需求。故填F。

subject: english
content: We should keep [[_]] (镇静的) whatever we face.
explanation: 句意：无论面对什么，我们都应该保持镇静。“镇静的”用calm表达，是形容词作表语。

subject: english
content: I [[_]] (注意到) a small bird in the tree just now.
explanation: 句意：刚才我注意到树上有一只小鸟。“注意到”用notice表达，根据时间状语just now“刚才”可知，句子是一般过去时，动词要用过去式，notice的过去式是noticed。

subject: english
content: My sister has many [[_]] (昆虫) in her collection box.
explanation: 句意：我妹妹的收藏盒里有许多昆虫。句中“many”后需接可数名词复数形式，括号内提示“昆虫”对应的英文单词为insect，其复数形式为insects。

subject: english
content: She often helps her mother do some [[_]] (家务) at home.
explanation: 句意：她经常在家帮妈妈做家务。“housework” 和“chores”都有“家务”的意思。housework是不可数名词，do some housework 是固定搭配，泛指做家务劳动；chore是可数名词复数，do some chores也是固定搭配，指做各类具体的家务杂活。此处两个表达均可。

subject: english
content: My daughter likes eating [[_]] (汉堡包).
explanation: 句意：我女儿喜欢吃汉堡包。“汉堡包”的英文是hamburger，是可数名词；句中表示一类事物，要用复数形式hamburgers，符合语境和语法要求。

subject: english
content: I’m p[[_]] to say that I’m from one of the most beautiful places in the world.
explanation: 句意：我很自豪地说，我来自世界上最美丽的地方之一。 根据提示首字母p和固定搭配be proud to do sth.（自豪地做某事），结合句中“来自世界上最美丽的地方之一”的语境，此处应填proud。

subject: english
content: The dish tastes very d[[_]]. We all love it.
explanation: 句意：这道菜尝起来非常美味。我们都很喜欢。根据“We all love it”和首字母可知，此处表示食物好吃，delicious“美味的”符合语境。故填delicious。

content:
我们对现实世界充耳不闻。

We are [[_]] [[_]] the real world .

content:
乐趣可以摆脱不良情绪，提振我们的精神。

Fun can do away with bad feelings and [[_]] our [[_]].

content:
在日常生活中尽量说英语。

Try to speak English in your [[_]].
explanation: 原句中“日常生活”是关键词，“日常生活”用daily life表达；在日常生活中用“in one’s daily life”表达，句子是祈使句，隐含的主语是you，此处one’s替换成your。

subject: english
content:
请从方框内选择适当的词并用其正确形式填空，使文章完整连贯。注意每空一词，每词仅用一次，有两词为多余项。

feel 、and 、be 、help 、good 、choose 、but 、hungry 、stay 、healthy 、vegetable 、fall

Every morning, Sarah starts her day with a [[46]] breakfast. She always chooses oatmeal (燕麦粥) with a glass of milk. “This gives me energy (能量) to [[47]] active all morning!” she says.

At lunchtime, Sarah packs her own meal. She includes a sandwich made with whole grain bread, plenty of [[48]]. “I try to avoid too much junk food,” she explains.

After school, Sarah sometimes feels [[49]]. Instead of eating chips or candy, she [[50]]a piece of fruit or yogurt. “These snacks are [[51]] for me and still taste great!”

For dinner, Sarah’s family eat together. They often have fish or chicken with steamed (蒸的) vegetables [[52]] brown rice. Sarah’s mom says, “Eating healthy food [[53]] important for growing bodies.” Before bed, Sarah drinks a glass of water. She knows staying hydrated (保持水分的) [[54]] her feel great the next day.

Sarah [[55]] great and energetic because of her eating habits. “Healthy food makes me happy and ready to learn!” she says.
explanation:
句意：每天早上，Sarah以一份健康的早餐开启她的一天。“with a…breakfast”修饰名词breakfast，结合下文提到的燕麦粥和牛奶等健康食品，此处应填形容词表示“健康的”。

句意：她说：“这给了我一整个上午保持活跃的能量！”“to…active”中，active是形容词，前面需要一个系动词来表示保持某种状态。选项框中的stay（保持）常与形容词连用，构成stay active（保持活跃）。

句意：她的午餐包括一个全麦面包三明治和大量的蔬菜。“plenty of”后接可数名词复数或不可数名词。根据健康饮食的搭配，三明治里通常会有蔬菜。选项框中的vegetable（蔬菜）在此处应用复数形式vegetables。

句意：放学后，Sarah有时会感到饥饿。“feels”是系动词，后接形容词作表语。根据后半句“Instead of eating chips or candy...”（而不是吃薯片或糖果……）推断，她是因为饿了才想吃东西。

句意：她不吃薯片糖果，而是选择吃一块水果或酸奶。“she…a piece of fruit”，句子缺少谓语动词。根据上下文，这是她在做选择。选项框中的choose（选择）符合语境，且主语she是第三人称单数，故填chooses。

句意：“这些零食对我有好处，而且味道也很棒！”“These snacks are…”，be动词后接形容词。既然Sarah坚持吃水果坚果而不吃垃圾食品，说明她认为这些零食是好的。

句意：他们经常吃鱼肉或鸡肉，搭配蒸蔬菜和糙米。空格连接并列的食物，需用并列连词，方框中“and”符合此语法功能。

句意：Sarah的妈妈说：“吃健康的食物对成长中的身体很重要。”主语是动名词短语，视为单数，需用be动词“is”，构成“be important for”表示“对……重要”。

句意：她知道保持水分能帮助她第二天感觉很棒。“Sleep and exercise can…her feel great...”，情态动词can后接动词原形。选项框中的help（帮助）符合语境。

句意：因为她的饮食习惯，Sarah感觉很棒，精力充沛。句子缺少谓语动词，主语“Sarah”是第三人称单数，方框中“feel”需变为第三人称单数形式“feels”，意为“感觉”。

subject: english
material:

It is the day of the school trip at Rainbow Middle School. The students wear their uniforms and take the school bus to the zoo.

When they arrive, they first see a playful fox. When they get close, it just runs away. Mrs Gao tells the students that foxes have very good hearing. They can hear people coming from far away.

Then they notice some animals with long necks looking at them. Can you guess what they are? Yes, they’re giraffes. Some students want to feed them, but they don’t do that. They know it’s the rule.

Later, they see a snake. Mrs Gao says, “This kind of snake is very dangerous. You may be in great danger if you stand close to it.” So all of them watch it at a safe distance (距离).

After that, Mrs Gao gives the students sandwiches to eat. Then Mrs Gao asks, “Do you still remember the rule—no littering?” “Yes, of course!” Mrs Gao feels happy to hear that.

On the trip, the students learn a lot about animals. They wish to visit the zoo again.
answer: To the zoo./They go to the zoo.
explanation: 根据第一段中“take the school bus to the zoo”可知，旅行目的地是动物园。

Lynn Jenner quickly packed up and drove to higher ground as Hurricane Hone approached in 2024. However, he wasn’t relocating his family; he was shifting snails.

Jenner works with some of the rarest endangered species on the planet — Hawaii’s native tree snails. Once abundant like Christmas ornaments on trees, these colorful, jewel-like snails are now mostly extinct with more than half of the 750 species vanishing within the span of a human lifetime. Jenner and his team with Hawaii’s Department of Land and Natural Resources face the monumental task of saving what’s left.

To beat extinction, 40 species of snails, each about the size of a dime, are being cared for by humans in an unremarkable trailer near Honolulu. “Most people think of pandas and tigers when they think of endangered species going extinct, but imagine having 40 different species that are all as rare as pandas.” Jenner says.

This winter, one species of snail will reach a significant milestone. It will be released in a special enclosure in the mountains of Oahu, which has been painstakingly prepared to give the snails the best chance of survival in their natural habitat.

However, the outlook for Hawaii’s snails remain uncertain. Around the globe, plants and animals are being brought into enclosure as a last-ditch effort against extinction. But with climate change and the spread of invasive species, many have no clear path back to the wild in the near term. This could mean they will remain under human care. In light of the biodiversity crisis, many wildlife biologists believe there’s no other option. “These are irreplaceable biological treasures,” Jenner says. “It is now or never. What we manage to preserve on Earth will be what the next generation can reintroduce.”
content: What does the text say about Hawaii’s tree snails?
options: They live as long as humans.

A watched pot never boils, but time has wings when you’re having fun. The familiar saying has a basis in solid science — our sense of time does expand and contract depending on the way we experience the world. Even delicate visual features can affect how we perceive time. New research shows more memorable images seem to last longer.

Martin Wiener, head of the research, says the finding helps reveal how the brain’s time-bending strategy allows it to process and remember more information. While what is actually happening in the brain when time seems to expand remains unclear, scientists suspect it may have something to do with helping the brain process more information in limited time.

This is especially relevant to the brain’s visual system which, subjected to information overload, has to rank in order of importance, allowing for limited resources. Recent research has shown some images are more naturally memorable than others.

To understand how this memorability of an image, along with a few simpler visual features such as scene size and disorder, might relate to our subjective sense of time, Wiener and his colleagues conducted related experiments, in which subjects were shown images with varying durations and were asked to categorize whether the length of time on the screen was either “short” or “long”. The next day they were given a surprise memory test to see which images they recalled seeing.

The researchers found larger scene sizes seemed to extend time while more disorderly scenes seemed to reduce the perceived duration. Besides, the subjects perceived that more memorable images remained on the screen longer, even if they were all presented for the same amount of time. To find the underlying factor, the team fed the same memorability-ranked images to a neural (神经的) network modeled after the brain’s visual system and found more memorable images were processed faster.

The explanation for why our brain’s faster processing would slow time is that it’s increasing the amount of information it can take in at once. Limited resources to process information may act as a sort of bottleneck, which the brain can widen when it needs to absorb more information, thus dilating time.
content: What does the familiar saying “A watched pot never boils” illustrate?
options: Actively waiting makes time feel slower.
Visual features are the key to judging time.
Our activities do not change time perception.
Time perception relies mainly on emotional state.

Many people count on faster, cheaper and better technology to offer a vision of a brighter future. Nevertheless, as the 2020s dawn, optimism is in short supply. The new technologies that dominated the past decade seem to be making matters worse. Social media, intended to connect people, are infamous for privacy leaks. Convenient E-commerce and on-demand ride services are charged with underpaying workers and blocking the streets with vehicles.

Today’s pessimistic mood targets smart phones and social media, which took off a decade ago. Yet concerns that particular technologies might be doing more harm than good have arisen before. The 1920s witnessed a criticism of cars, once regarded as solutions to horse-drawn vehicles issues like noise, waste, and accidents. And industrialization was criticized in the 19th century by Romanticism who worried about the replacement of skilled workers, the robbing of the countryside and the suffering of factory hands.

However, that pessimism can be overdone. Too often people focus on the drawbacks of a new technology while taking its benefits for granted. Worries about screen time should be weighed against the much more substantial benefits of instant communication and information access that smartphones make possible. A further danger is that Luddites’ (卢德分子) efforts to avoid the short-term costs associated with a new technology will end up denying access to its long-term benefits — something Carl Benedict Frey, an Oxford academic, calls a “technology trap”. Fears that robots will steal people’s jobs may discourage their use. Yet in the long run countries that wish to maintain their living standard as their workforce ages and decreases will need more robots, not fewer.

Any powerful technology can be used for good or ill. It is the choices people make about it that shape the world. Perhaps the real source of anxiety is not technology itself, but growing doubts about the ability of societies to hold this debate, and come up with good answers. So as the decade turns, put aside the pessimism for a moment. To be alive in the tech-fascinated 2020s is to be among the luckiest people who have ever lived.
content: Which may be a problem caused by social media in paragraph 1?

Yet in the long run countries that wish to maintain their living standard as their workforce ages and decreases will need more robots, not fewer.

Any powerful technology can be used for good or ill. It is the choices people make about it that shape the world. Perhaps the real source of anxiety is not technology itself, but growing doubts about the ability of societies to hold this debate, and come up with good answers. So as the decade turns, put aside the pessimism for a moment. To be alive in the tech-fascinated 2020s is to be among the luckiest people who have ever lived.

Beyond Technological Pessimism: Society’s choices matter.
The Technology Trap: An Unavoidable Dilemma.

content:
阅读下面材料, 根据其内容和所给段落开头语续写两段, 使之构成一篇完整的短文。

Mrs. Peabody was a serious old woman the kids called psychic (通灵者) because she magically knew which students had accomplished the real assignment and which had not.

She once gave the class a writing assignment. “Write an essay about summer vacation. ”she said. “Be as creative as you can. ”

Well, that night Jim sat at his desk at home and stared unhappily at a blank sheet of paper. He didn’t want to write a stupid essay about his summer vacation. Boring. So he gave up on the assignment but wrote what he wanted to—not an essay at all but a science fiction. It was about a distant planet that didn’t have summer—it was spring all the time. And it didn’t have vacations either. The aliens on the planet worked 24 hours a day.

The next morning he handed in the story but that night he lay awake until three a. m. , thinking: Why did I do that? I totally ignored the assignment. Maybe it’d take Mrs. Peabody a few days to grade the essays. I’d beg her for a chance to write another one, the sort she wanted.

But when he got to class the next morning it turned out that Mrs. Peabody had read and graded the essays. And when he saw the way she glanced at him with a strange look in her sten, psychic eyes, he wished he’d stayed home sick. I’m in trouble, Jim thought, blushing already, betrayed by his freckles (雀斑). Staring at the floor. Mrs. Peabody continued, “Almost everyone in class wrote an essay about his or her summer vacation . Almost everyone. ”This is bad, Jim thought. I’m getting an F, I know it. “But, ” the teacher said, “One student decided he didn’t feel like doing that. ” Jim glanced up long enough to see her eyes focused on him. This is worse than an F. . . I’m in note-to-the-parents territory now.

Then Jim heard his name called.

_________________________________

_________________________________

_________________________________

_________________________________

When Jim finished reading his story, a smile spread across Mrs. Peabody’s face.

_________________________________

_________________________________

_________________________________

_________________________________
answer: 【参考例文】 Then Jim heard his name called. His heart raced. Slowly he walked to the front, ready to accept punishment. To his surprise, Mrs. Peabody handed his paper back and asked him to read his work aloud. Nervous as he was, Jim took a deep breath and began to read the sci-fi story about the alien planet. He could feel all classmates’ eyes fixed on him. When Jim finished reading his story, a smile spread across Mrs. Peabody’s face. She told the whole class that creativity mattered more than following the task strictly. She praised Jim’s wild imagination and interesting plot. Though he didn’t write the required essay, his creative story was excellent. Jim let out a big sigh of relief. He learned that thinking outside the box could be a great gift.

subject: english
material:
阅读短文，用英文填空或回答问题。(注意每小题的词数要求)

Imagine you have no phone, no map, and no one to ask for help. How would you know where to go? For thousands of years, humans have found clever methods to take directions.

One simple way is to watch the sky. East is where the sun rises, and west is where it sets. That is the simplest sign. At night, ancient Chinese depended on the stars. The most useful one is the North Star. It stays almost still in the northern sky. Travelers followed it along their journeys across the desert. Sailors(水手) once used it to guide their ships on the sea.

Nature offers you signs to read. For example, moss(苔藓) grows thicker on the wet dark north side of trees. That’s why in the forests of North America, hunters can easily tell the north is on the mossy side.

Man-made marks are left to help. In the snowy Arctic, local people built stone statues(雕塑)—shaped like a person—as special signs. Travelers who saw one would know the right way. Even today, people still build them as marks or works of art.

Tools give people a hand. About 2,500 years ago, the Chinese made sinan. It was often used to help people build houses facing south. During the Northern Song Dynasty, the compass(指南针) was invented. Sailors used it at sea to find their way and return home safely. Later, the compass spread to Europe. It was improved and used to explore unknown oceans and find new lands.

Even long before modern technologies, people all over the world knew where they were going.

Guide: It stays almost still and points north.

Read signs in nature

Situation: [[48]]

Guide: It shows the north is on the mossy side.

Notice special marks

Situation: in the snowy Arctic

Sign: a stone statue

Guide: It [[47]].

Depend on tools

Situation: at sea

Sign: [[49]]

Guide: It tells where the south is.

由第二段的“One simple way is to watch the sky”可知，第一种方法是在晴朗的夜晚观察天空。watch the sky表示“观察天空”，空处与“Read signs in nature” “ Notice special marks”和“Depend on tools”并列，故填Watch the sky。

由第三段的“in the forests of North America, hunters can easily tell the north is on the mossy side”可知，在北美洲的森林中可以通过苔藓辨别方向。故填in the forests of North America。

由第四段的“Travelers who saw one would know the right way.”可知，石像向旅行者指明正确方向。故填shows the right way。

由第五段的“During the Northern Song Dynasty, the compass(指南针) was invented. Sailors used it at sea to find their way”可知，水手在海上使用指南针。故填the compass。

6 days Philippine: Manila to Bohol Tour

Discover Philippines on this 6-day tour through Manila and the island of Bohol.

Day1

Fly from your origin city and arrive in the lively Philippine capital of Manila. Upon arrival, transfer to your centrally located hotel to check-in and relax after your flight.

Day2

This morning, take a scenic drive south of Manila to Tagaytay Ridge for amazing views of Taal Lake and Volcano. Stop first at People’s Park. After lunch, take a boat ride on breathtaking Taal Lake, the smallest volcano in the world. Return to Manila in the late afternoon.

Day3

Transfer to Manila airport for your short flight to Bohol. Upon arrival, our guide will take you on a countryside tour. First, take a one-hour Loboc River cruise, passing through forests and villages. Next visit the famous 16th-century Baclayon Church. After that, you will visit Chocolate Hills, and enjoy striking views of limestone cliffs (石灰岩峭壁) and rolling hills from the viewpoint. Return to your resort in the late afternoon.

Day4

Today enjoy fun water activities on the nearby islands. Start with a dolphin watching boat tour to Balicasag Island for a lunch stop. Spend the afternoon snorkeling (潜水). Also tour Virgin Island with time on the powder white sand beach. Return to Bohol in the evening.

Day5

Transfer to Tagbilaran airport for your flight to Manila. On arrival in Manila, set off on a tour of cultural highlights in the capital. First, admire Rizal Park and the Manila Cathedral. Next, explore the UNESCO-listed walled city of Intramuros. Return to your hotel in the late afternoon.

Day6

You are free until your departure flight home from Manila International Airport. Transfer to the airport for your onward international flight.

Price

5990 RMB Regular

Price include

√Airport transfer between Manila International Airport and hotels

√Experienced English-speaking local tour guides for all scheduled trips

√Transportation throughout the tour

√Hotel accommodation in 4-star comfortable hotels based on twin sharing

√Entry tickets to all included cultural and historical sites

√Daily breakfast

√One Lunch

Price exclude

×International and domestic flights

×Tips for guides and drivers

×Philippine Visa

×Travel insurance
content: Which day features a trip to the countryside?
explanation: 细节理解题。根据Day 3部分“Upon arrival, our guide will take you on a countryside tour”, 可知，第三天安排了乡村之旅。故选B。

subject: english
material:
In 1996, someone ate a McDonald’s McChicken burger in Amsterdam. We don’t know the details, but something important happened. A nesting coot, a kind of bird, found the abandoned (丢弃的) wrapper and used it to line its nest (巢). That wrapper stayed there, leaving a mark on the local environment.

Biologist Auke-Florian Hiemstra studies how people affect bird nests in Amsterdam’s canals (运河). He said birds are also “recording” our throw-away society. When he looked at nests in the canals, he found all kinds of old packaging from the early 1990s to last year.

The Eurasian coot started coming to Amsterdam in the late 1980s. The packaging in the nests, like the 1996 McChicken wrapper, can show how long the species has been in the area. Hiemstra can tell the year of the packaging by looking at “best before” dates or logo designs. Nests have things like Mars bar packaging from the 1994 World Cup and, more recently, face masks from the pandemic.

Birds usually make nests from branches and plants. But in cities, there aren’t many natural things. So, birds use a lot of plastic. Hiemstra thinks if we make cities greener, birds might go back to making natural nests.

Hiemstra is upset about our “throw-away society”. Most plastic we make is still on Earth because it takes 20 to 500 years to decompose, and only 9% is recycled. We know single-use plastic is bad, but this research shows it’s already caused a lot of damage.
content: What does the discovery of the McChicken wrapper in the coot’s nest imply?
options: The coot is an intelligent bird species.
Amsterdam has a serious litter problem.
It reflects the throwaway nature of human society.
Birds have a preference for human-made materials.
explanation: 推理判断题。根据第二段“He said birds are also ‘recording’ our throw-away society. When he looked at nests in the canals, he found all kinds of old packaging”, 可知，鸟巢中的麦香鸡包装纸反映了人类社会的一次性消费本质。故选C。

subject: english
material:
I like scrolling (滚屏) through social media more than posting. It’s my daily way to relax. Before, my feed was full of perfect tiny homes, making me dream of a minimalist life. But then, AI-generated images with obvious flaws (瑕疵) showed up. Some had staircases going nowhere, and some had sinks inside sinks. Strangely, few commenters pointed these out. They just praised the overall look. It made me wonder: did people not spot (发现) these mistakes, or did they not care?

I study how people understand visual information. Our eyes aren’t great at spotting small details when we casually scroll. We usually just get the big picture and miss the little things that don’t match. Our visual attention is like a zoom lens (变焦镜头). We scan things quickly, and focusing on details takes extra effort.

Our ability to sense things evolved to spot dangers fast in nature, choosing speed over precision. This was good for early humans, but not for modern scrolling. So, small errors in AI-generated images often go unnoticed.

There’s also something called in attentional blindness. When we focus on one thing, we overlook other details, even if they’re obvious. Just like in the famous invisible gorilla (大猩猩) study. People counting basketball passes didn’t notice a person in a gorilla suit walking by. Similarly, when we look at an AI image, we might miss its flaws while focusing on the main part.

Our thinking has two types: fast and intuitive (凭直觉的), and slow and analytical. When scrolling, the fast-thinking part usually takes charge, making us accept images easily. Also, we tend to accept information that fits our beliefs and ignore the rest. So, AI-generated images that match what we expect can fool us. For pictures of tiny homes, the flaws might not matter much. But when AI-generated images are used to influence public opinion, it’s a big problem. Research shows people often assume images support the text, even if there’s no real proof. Misleading images can make false things seem true. AI-generated images can spread wrong information, and it’s hard to stop. To avoid being misled, we should slow down, look closely, and think carefully.
content: What is the main purpose of the first paragraph?
options: To display the diversity of social media content.
To introduce the author’s daily social media habits.
To explain the popularity of Al-generated images on social media.
To present the author’s concern about public reactions to AI-generated images.
explanation: 推理判断题。根据第一段“Strangely, few commenters pointed these out... It made me wonder: did people not spot these mistakes, or did they not care?”, 可知，第一段旨在呈现作者对公众对AI生成图像反应的担忧。故选D。

subject: english
material:
How to Become a Super Learner

Becoming a super learner is essential for success in the 21st century. In a rapidly changing world, the ability to learn new skills quickly is a must. The good news is, anyone can be a super learner with the right methods.[[1]] Many famous polymaths (博学者) claimed not to have extraordinary natural intelligence, proving that with the right tools, we all can master new disciplines.

Super learners read a lot

Reading is as important to the mind as exercise is to the body. [[2]] It allows our minds to explore various aspects of the world and enriches our understanding of different ideas. Successful people like Elon Musk, Bill Gates, and others read a lot because they see it as a way to improve their lives and careers. In a world where information is valuable, reading is the best way to continuously learn and gain knowledge.

Super learners view learning as a process

Learning is a journey, not a destination. [[3]] It’s an enjoyable lifelong process that requires curiosity. Super learners don’t focus on an end goal but seek consistent improvement, constantly mastering new things. This ongoing pursuit (追求) of knowledge is key to their growth.

Super learners teach others what they know

Teaching others is one of the most effective ways to learn. [[4]] When we teach, we manage to remember about 90%of what we’ve learned. The Feynman Technique, for example, emphasizes learning by teaching simply. Sharing what we’ve learned helps us identify knowledge gaps and strengthen our memory.

Super learners take short breaks, early and often

[[5]] Research shows that frequent breaks can improve learning and memory. Our brains need time to process information, so spacing out learning sessions with breaks helps us memorize new knowledge more efficiently.

By adopting these habits, you can become a super learner and thrive in this ever-changing world.
options: It is a continuous and progressing experience.
It activates our brain, making new connections and patterns.
Resting is as important as practicing when it comes to learning.
You don’t need to be naturally gifted to learn new skills effectively.
What we eat and do can affect how our brain processes information.
With a growth mindset, we focus better on our goals and be more motivated.
Sharing knowledge not only benefits others but also enhances our own learning.
explanation: 空格前指出任何人通过正确方法都能成为超级学习者，后文提到博学者称自己没有非凡天赋，证明用对工具就能掌握新学科。选项D“要有效学习新技能，你不需要天生有天赋”承上启下，呼应前后文内容，符合语境。故选D。

subject: english
content:
In recent years, there [[1]] (be) a great increase in people’s interest in museums. This enthusiasm has given rise to a trend in cultural and creative [[2]] (product) young people like, especially fridge magnets (冰箱贴) modeled [[3]] real museum items.

These museum-inspired refrigerator magnets have caught the imagination of many and become [[4]] popular type in cultural and creative goods. For example, the “Phoenix Crown Magnet” [[5]] (fashion) by the National Museum of China has quickly gained popularity among young people. Within three months, more than 530,000 of these magnets have been sold, making [[6]] the museum’s most sought-after product in nearly two decades. The crown magnet is designed according to a crown worn by Empress Xiaoduan of the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644), [[7]] is a beautiful headpiece decorated with more than 500 red and blue stones and over a thousand pearls. The magnets come in both wood and metal styles, and [[8]] (create) carefully to reflect the original design.

[[9]] (addition), the “Heavenly Palace Caisson Magnet” from the Beijing Ancient Architecture Museum and the “Qianlong Imperial Pavilion Sand and Leaf Magnet” from the Beijing Art Museum have also won the hearts of lovers. These cultural refrigerator magnets serve as precious reminders of people’s trips and expressions of [[10]] (they) love for culture.
explanation:
考查时态和主谓一致。“in recent years”表明用现在完成时，主语“a great increase”是单数，助动词用has。故填has been。

考查名词复数。“product”是可数名词，此处指多种文化创意产品，用复数形式。故填products。

考查介词。“modeled after”是固定短语，意为“以……为原型”。故填after。

考查冠词。“type”是可数名词，此处表泛指，“popular”以辅音音素开头，用不定冠词a。故填a。

考查非谓语动词。“fashion”与“Phoenix Crown Magnet”是被动关系，用过去分词作定语。故填fashioned。

考查代词。用it指代前文的“Phoenix Crown Magnet”。故填it。

考查定语从句。先行词是“a crown”, 指物，在非限制性定语从句中作主语，用which引导。故填which。

考查时态和语态。“magnets”与“create”是被动关系，结合前文“come”, 可知用一般现在时的被动语态，主语是复数，be动词用are。故填are created。

考查副词。此处用副词修饰整个句子，“addition”的副词形式是“additionally”, 句首首字母大写。故填Additionally。

考查代词。修饰名词“love”, 用形容词性物主代词“their”。故填their。

Last weekend, I signed up for a community volunteer activity to clean and beautify the local park with several classmates. In the morning, we gathered at the park entrance, equipped with trash bags and gloves. The park, once a lively place, now was messy with rubbish everywhere.

As we spread out to handle the mess, my attention was drawn to a boy standing near a stone bench. His old jacket hung loosely on his thin body, as if it had been worn for a long time. He looked around nervously, like a scared animal watching for danger. Suddenly, he moved quickly, grabbing something shiny from the bench and putting it into his pocket. My heart stopped when I realized it was a smooth, silver watch with a leather strap (皮带)—clearly a valuable item.

I knew the boy had taken the watch. My first thought was to go to him directly and point out his serious moral (道德上的) mistake, for it was everyone’s responsibility to stand up for honesty and fairness. But when I looked at the boy, I saw fear and hopelessness in his eyes. He was a poor kid, maybe no more than ten years old. I couldn’t help wondering what difficulties might have made him do this. If I reported him to the park office, he might get into serious trouble, maybe negatively affecting his young life. But if I ignored it, it would mean allowing his bad behavior, which went against my belief. I stood there, feeling a strong moral conflict.

Just then, the park office began to broadcast, looking for a lost watch. At that, the boy hesitated for a moment, and then disappeared somewhere before I knew it.

I shook my head and began to work, but my mind was still on the boy and the watch. That evening, as I lay in bed, the boy’s scared face kept coming to my mind, and I still hadn’t decided what to do.

When I arrived at the park the next day, I saw the boy sitting alone on the same bench, even more upset.

______________________________________________________________________

______________________________________________________________________

______________________________________________________________________

We went to the park office at once, telling them we had found a watch.

______________________________________________________________________

______________________________________________________________________

______________________________________________________________________

<u style="text-emphasis">When I arrived at the park the next day, I saw the boy sitting alone on the same bench, even more upset.</u> He looked around nervously as if expecting someone. I approached and said gently “I noticed what happened here yesterday. Can you tell me about it?” His face turned pale. “I... I took that watch,” he whispered with shame, staring at his worn clothes. “I envied other kids’ decent jackets and just wanted to buy one.” Moved by his honesty, I advised him to hand it in to the staff member. He nodded, admitting he’d felt guilty ever since and came back to return the watch.
<u style="text-emphasis">We went to the park office at once, telling them we had found a watch.</u> Seeing the watch, a staff member smiled kindly and praised the boy for his honesty. Then she gave him some money, saying it was a reward from the owner. Feeling embarrassed, he pushed it back, saying “I just want to earn money by myself.” The staff member nodded, offering him a part-time job to collect trash during weekends. As we left, the boy’s face was no longer filled with fear but a newfound resolve, and a bit of hope.

subject: english
material:
Frank Caprio is a well-known judge who has gained popularity for his caring and understanding approach in the courtroom. Born on November 23, 1936, Caprio serves as the Chief Judge of the Providence Municipal Court in Rhode Island, USA.

His trials have been turned into a television program called “Caught in Providence”, which airs on local Fox stations and presents his work.

Caprio’s decisions often reflect a mixture of legal strictness and human warmth. He is known for his merciful judgments and his ability to connect with the people before him. For instance, in one case, a 96-year-old man was brought before Caprio for speeding in a school zone. The elderly man explained that he was driving his 63-year-old son, who has cancer, to a blood test. After hearing the man’s story, Caprio responded with sympathy, highlighting the man’s dedication to his family at an advanced age.

Judge Caprio has been called “the warmest judge” by his admirers because of his way of handling justice. His trials prove that the law can be applied with understanding and mercy, which has made him a beloved figure both in the United States and around the world.

Another heartwarming example is that Caprio once canceled a double fine for a truck driver who hadn’t got a notice for a previous fine. After the case was dismissed, the driver shared that 20 years ago, as a lost teenager, Caprio had asked him about his future dreams during a trial, a question that marked a turning point in the driver’s life.

Caprio’s story is not just about his role as a judge but also about how a single kind act can affect someone’s life. His way of working as a judge shows that justice can be done with sympathy and that sometimes a kind word can change a person’s path for the better.
content: What makes Frank Caprio popular?
options: His appearances in a TV program.
His ability to solve complex legal cases.
His balance of mercy and justice in trials.
His strict legal decisions in the courtroom.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据第一段“... caring and understanding approach”及第四段“... law can be applied with understanding and mercy”可知，他受欢迎的原因是审判中平衡了仁慈与正义。A选项（电视节目露面）是其影响力的体现，而非原因；B、D选项与原文描述相反。故选C。

subject: english
material:
Meat, milk, cheese — just some of the things provided by goats. But now we can also add fire safety to this list. As wildfires damage increasingly large areas of the planet each year, goatherds (牧羊人) may offer a way of reducing the risk.

Wildfires are made possible by hot, dry weather conditions as well as a supply of dead plants that serve as fuel. We may have limited control over the former factor, but we can control the latter. Reducing the fuel load lowers the possibility of wildfires occurring, as well as the amount of damage caused. This is where we can turn to goats to search for a solution, which are being used for landscape management in a number of places around the world, including Greece, Spain, Portugal, Chile and a number of parts of the United States.

Goats have an extremely powerful digestive (消化的) system. Many kinds of plants that are dangerous to other animals can be easily eaten by goats. It’s not just fully-grown plants that goats are able to deal with: any seeds that pass through a goat can’t survive and will not grow. Human clearance teams have to worry about getting to the hard-to-reach places where plants grow but goats don’t. They are skilled mountain climbers and when standing on their hind legs, they can reach up to two metres to the plants that humans would struggle to reach. Because of this, using goats can reduce both the possibility of workplace accidents and the amount of money spent on fire protection measures. Goatherds have been found to clear some parts of land for a third of the price of human control teams.

Cost and safety aren’t the only benefits. Goats are quieter than grass-cutting machines and people usually prefer to see goats eating grass rather than litres of herbicide (除草剂). Children are often attracted to see the goats at work and this provides an opportunity to educate people about preventing wildfires.
content: Why can goats help to prevent wildfires?
options: They are not afraid of bad weather.
They are easily controlled by goatherds.
They have the strongest digestive system.
They can remove dead plants causing fire.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据第二段“... dead plants that serve as fuel”和“turn to goats to search for a solution”可知，山羊通过清除作为燃料的枯死植物来预防野火。A选项（不怕坏天气）、B（易被控制）文中未提及；C选项（最强消化系统）是能力，而非直接原因。故选D。

subject: english
material:
Have you ever played a computer game for a long time and then kept seeing its images afterward? This happened to me with the classic game Tetris (俄罗斯方块).

Feeling stressed one evening, I decided to find a game to relax with. That’s when I discovered Tetris. Before I knew it, I was obsessed. My brain was still playing, with the blocks falling in my mind. I started looking at objects in the real world, imagining how they could be moved and fit together like the game’s blocks. I even dreamed about Tetris. I was experiencing what’s known as the “Tetris effect”.

Introduced by journalist Jeffrey Goldsmith in his article called “This Is Your Brain on Tetris”, the effect has been observed by psychologists and researchers. The lasting images of Tetris are due to the “Zeigarnik effect”, in which people have better memories of uncompleted tasks than those of completed ones. Tetris, being a game that technically never ends, keeps you thinking of the game’s unfinished task, reported Tech Times. And the catchy music stays with you, too.

Interestingly, the Tetris effect has some positive aspects. In 1991, psychologist Richard Haier at the University of California found that continuously playing Tetris resulted in the thickness of the cerebral cortex (大脑皮层) increasing, which improves brain efficiency, reported psychology website Practical Pie. Haier’s discovery got Tetris put into the Guinness World Records Video Gamer’s Edition 2008, as the “first video game to be proven to improve brain functioning and efficiency”.

Tetris has also been researched for its potential as a treatment for trauma. In a study at John Radcliffe Hospital in Oxford, researchers found that playing Tetris helped reduce unwanted memories in people who had been in car accidents.

So, the next time you want to play a computer game, why not try the classic Tetris and see if it improves your brain function? But be warned, you’ll likely be seeing falling blocks everywhere.
content: What does the underlined word “obsessed” in paragraph 2 probably mean?
explanation: 词义猜测题。根据后文“... brain was still playing” “dreamed about Tetris”可知，作者对俄罗斯方块“极度着迷”，obsessed意为“痴迷的”，与D选项“Extremely interested”同义。A（震惊）、B（好奇）、C（满足）均不符合沉迷游戏的语境。故选D。

In 1991, psychologist Richard Haier at the University of California found that continuously playing Tetris resulted in the thickness of the cerebral cortex (大脑皮层) increasing, which improves brain efficiency, reported psychology website Practical Pie. material:
Have you ever played a computer game for a long time and then kept seeing its images afterward? This happened to me with the classic game Tetris (俄罗斯方块).

Feeling stressed one evening, I decided to find a game to relax with. That’s when I discovered Tetris. Before I knew it, I was obsessed. Haier’s discovery got Tetris put into the Guinness World Records Video Gamer’s Edition 2008, as the “first video game to be proven to improve brain functioning and efficiency”.

Tetris has also been researched for its potential as a treatment for trauma. In a study at John Radcliffe Hospital in Oxford, researchers found that playing Tetris helped reduce unwanted memories in people who had been in car accidents.

So, the next time you want to play a computer game, why not try the classic Tetris and see if it improves your brain function? But be warned, you’ll likely be seeing falling blocks everywhere.

material:

Preferences may vary, but a common truth is obvious: life couldn’t be lived without books.[[1]]

Created on April 23rd, 1995, by the United Nations, the day is all about celebrating the wonderful power of books and the joy of reading.[[2]]However, people of all ages can celebrate it in their own ways.

[[3]]Do you have a book you just can’t get around to finish? Why not curl up on the couch and enjoy every last page? If you have children, pick a topic they’re interested in and explore the magical world of literature together. It is the perfect day to teach them the joy of reading.

Yet it is also a good choice to get together with some friends and share the same book you all love. Hearing someone read aloud sentences you have only ever murmured to yourself could cause you to see them in a whole new way. [[4]]

Whichever way you choose to celebrate World Book Day, it’s an educational experience. [[5]]They are a door into another world, full of fiction and imagination or facts that teach you incredible new things.

A common celebration is doing some reading.
That’s why World Book Day is a well-deserved holiday.
Doing some reading helps you understand the world better.
It’s especially meant to encourage a love of reading in children.
Additionally, varied understanding of a book allows heated discussions.

Chinese traditional instruments have long charmed the world with their unique sounds and cultural significance. From erhu and pipa, [[1]] have gained international recognition, to lesser-known instruments that [[2]] (value) for their unique sounds and historical depth, these instruments have played an important role in China’s rich and diverse [[3]] (music) tradition.

Whether you are a seasoned musician or simply someone [[4]] (interest) in experiencing the beauty of traditional Chinese music, these instruments are sure [[5]] (amaze) and delight. From the delicate melodies of guqin and xiao to the rhythmic beats of drum and gong, there is something [[6]] everyone. [[7]] these instruments may seem mysterious and unfamiliar to some, they are [[8]] (surprising) not difficult to learn and can provide a lifetime of [[9]] (enjoy). So if you’re looking to explore the world of traditional Chinese music, consider taking up one of these instruments. Who knows—you might just discover a passion that lasts a lifetime.

Today, these instruments are making a strong comeback, [[10]] (bridge) ancient traditions with new ideas and creating music that feels both classic and fresh. By learning to play, you’re not just mastering melodies—you’re helping preserve a cultural treasure alive!
answer: (1) which；(2) are valued；(3) musical；(4) interested；(5) to amaze；(6) for；(7) Although/Though/While；(8) surprisingly；(9) enjoyment；(10) bridging
explanation:
考查定语从句。引导非限制性定语从句，先行词为erhu and pipa（指物），在从句中作主语，用关系代词which。故填which。

考查时态和语态。that引导定语从句，先行词instruments与value为被动关系，陈述客观事实用一般现在时，主语复数，be动词用are。故填are valued。

考查形容词。修饰名词tradition，用music的形容词形式musical（音乐的）。故填musical。

考查非谓语动词。someone与interest为被动关系，用过去分词interested作后置定语，表“感兴趣的”。故填interested。

考查连词。引导让步状语从句，表“尽管”，用Although/Though/While，首字母大写。故填Although/Though/While。

考查副词。修饰形容词difficult，用副词surprisingly（出人意料地）。故填surprisingly。

考查名词。a lifetime of后接名词enjoyment（乐趣）作宾语。故填enjoyment。

考查非谓语动词。instruments与bridge为主动关系，用现在分词bridging作伴随状语。故填bridging。

<u style="text-emphasis">Dear Tom,</u>
It’s great to hear you’re interested in Chinese historical stories! Let me share one called “Kong Rong Shared Pears.”
When Kong Rong was four, he and his brothers were given pears. While others took larger ones, Kong chose the smallest. Asked why, he replied, “I’m younger, so I should take the smaller one.” His family praised his humility, and this story has been passed down for centuries.
The story teaches the value of modesty and respect for elders. In a world where self-interest often dominates, Kong’s selflessness reminds us to prioritize harmony over personal gain. I believe such virtues remain essential today, especially in building trust within families and communities.
What do you think? Feel free to ask for more stories!
<u style="text-emphasis">Yours,</u>
<u style="text-emphasis">Li Hua</u>

material:
2025 Global Environment Solutions Challenge

Organizers:

Tongji University

Time:

From now until June 7, 2025

Place:

The first round is online. The semi-finals and final will be held in Shanghai.

Target Participants:

This challenge is open to all students from universities worldwide.

Requirements:

The entry (参赛作品) must be presented as a poster in PDF format with a resolution (分辨率) of at least 300 dpi. The poster has to clearly present the content. The work should be original. If you use other people’s material, you need to indicate the source.

Topics:

●Climate Action

Climate change and plastic pollution are two major environmental challenges today. Participants can put forward effective ideas from perspectives like the plastic life cycle, reducing carbon footprints, and climate adaptation strategies.

●Health Guardians

Microplastics entering the food chain can cause health problems. Participants can explore the potential risks of plastic pollution to human health and propose innovative solutions.

Award Setting:

The reward will be given to the team leader of the winning team. Shortlisted teams will be invited to Shanghai for the Semi-final competition.
content: Which of the following entries meets the requirements?
options: PDF, 200 dpi, by a US university student.
PDF, 350 dpi, handed in on June 1, 2025.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据Requirements部分“The entry must be presented as a poster in PDF format with a resolution of at least 300 dpi” 及Time部分“From now until June 7, 2025” 可知，D选项“PDF格式、350 dpi、2025年6月1日提交” 符合所有要求。故选D。

subject: english
material:
In 2024, Chinese doctor Wang Zhenyi, turning 100, was given the Medal of the Republic, China’s highest honor, for his battle against leukemia (白血病). Over decades, he transformed acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), a deadly disease, into one that can be cured.

In the mid-20th century, he saw about 60 APL patients die in a single year, which strengthened his determination to defeat leukemia. “As a doctor, it pains me most to see a patient suffering when there is nothing I can do,” he said.

Wang spent nearly all his free time in libraries and labs, doing research. After years of tireless work, an element called all-trans-retinoic acid (ATRA) came into the picture as a hopeful cure for APL.

In 1986, a five-year-old girl who was found to have APL was expected to die quickly. Wang used ATRA on her. Seven days later, her symptoms improved significantly; a month later, she fully recovered. That year, 24 APL patients were treated, and 23 of them got better without needing chemotherapy (化疗).

However, some patients later got sick again. To solve this, Wang added arsenic trioxide (ATO), a poisonous chemical. At first, the use of the poisonous compound was met with much doubt. However, it proved effective. With the new ATRA-ATO combination therapy (疗法), the survival rate for APL rose from 10 percent to more than 97 percent.

Wang refused to patent (申请专利) the therapy. “A doctor should put patients’ well-being first,” he said. Today, a box of 10 ATRA pills costs just 300 yuan in China.

Honored with national awards, Wang stayed modest, “I achieved only one thing — being responsible for my patients.”
content: What can we learn from the first two paragraphs?
options: APL made patients die without suffering.
Wang won the medal for his contributions.
APL was a mild disease before his research.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据第一段“In 2024, Chinese doctor Wang Zhenyi... was given the Medal of the Republic... for his battle against leukemia” 可知，王振义因对抗白血病的贡献获得勋章。故选B。

subject: english
material:
Humpback whale (座头鲸) songs follow patterns that are similar to human language, according to new studies. This suggests that features found throughout the animal kingdom may have guided the development of human speech.

Scientists aren’t sure exactly why humpbacks sing, but it seems to help them attract mates. As with human language, the whales’ songs are passed down culturally, meaning they are learned from others.

An international team of scientists studied recordings collected over eight years in the Pacific Ocean. Because humpback whale songs are made up of various sounds, the scientists created codes to describe different combinations of sounds. By figuring out which sounds often occurred together, they could find combinations in whale songs that served a purpose similar to words in a human speech.

When the researchers analyzed the whale songs using this method, they found that the songs followed a pattern, called Zipf’s law of frequency, that is also found in human language. Zipf’s law says that the most common word in a language is used twice as much as the second most common word, three times as much as the third most common word, and so on. For example, in English, the word “the” is used twice as often as “of” and three times as often as “and”.

“This made us realize that we’d uncovered a deep commonality between these two species, separated by millions of years of gradual development,” Simon Kirby, a University of Edinburgh researcher, told New Scientist.

Meanwhile, a separate study from Stony Brook University in New York found that the songs of humpbacks and blue whales use short words more often than longer ones, as is the case with human language. “Taken together, our studies suggest that humpback whale song has changed to be more efficient and easier to learn,” said the study’s author, Mason Yacht.
content: What can we learn about humpback whales from the first two paragraphs?
options: Their songs are used for social purposes.
They learn songs from other sea creatures.
Their songs have features similar to human language.
They have developed high intelligence close to human.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据第一段“Humpback whale songs follow patterns that are similar to human language, according to new studies.(新的研究表明，座头鲸的歌声遵循着与人类语言相似的模式。)”和第二段“As with human language, the whales’ songs are passed down culturally, meaning they are learned from others.(和人类语言一样，鲸鱼的歌声是通过文化传承下来的，也就是说它们是从其他鲸鱼那里学来的。)”可知，座头鲸的歌声有着和人类语言相似的特征。故选C。

Scientists aren’t sure exactly why humpbacks sing, but it seems to help them attract mates. As with human language, the whales’ songs are passed down culturally, meaning they are learned from others.

An international team of scientists studied recordings collected over eight years in the Pacific Ocean. Because humpback whale songs are made up of various sounds, the scientists created codes to describe different combinations of sounds. By figuring out which sounds often occurred together, they could find combinations in whale songs that served a purpose similar to words in a human speech.

When the researchers analyzed the whale songs using this method, they found that the songs followed a pattern, called Zipf’s law of frequency, that is also found in human language. Zipf’s law says that the most common word in a language is used twice as much as the second most common word, three times as much as the third most common word, and so on. For example, in English, the word “the” is used twice as often as “of” and three times as often as “and”.

“This made us realize that we’d uncovered a deep commonality between these two species, separated by millions of years of gradual development,” Simon Kirby, a University of Edinburgh researcher, told New Scientist.

Meanwhile, a separate study from Stony Brook University in New York found that the songs of humpbacks and blue whales use short words more often than longer ones, as is the case with human language. “Taken together, our studies suggest that humpback whale song has changed to be more efficient and easier to learn,” said the study’s author, Mason Yacht.
content: What can be a suitable title for the text?
options: Some whales sing like human speak.
Zipf’s law is the key feature in singing.
Whales sing louder than other animals.
explanation: 主旨大意题。根据第一段“Humpback whale songs follow patterns that are similar to human language, according to new studies.(新的研究表明，座头鲸的歌声遵循着与人类语言相似的模式。)”和最后一段“Meanwhile, a separate study from Stony Brook University in New York found that the songs of humpbacks and blue whales use short words more often than longer ones, as is the case with human language.(与此同时，纽约石溪大学的一项独立研究发现，座头鲸和蓝鲸的歌声中使用短词的频率要高于长词，这与人类语言的情况相同。)”及全文内容可知，文章主要讲述了座头鲸的歌声与人类语言的相似性。故选B。

subject: english
material:
Research has shown that consumers often would rather interact (互动) with human agents (代理人) than robotic ones. But a new study paints a more nuanced picture: When communicating a disappointing offer, a bot gets better results.

In one experiment, participants imagined that they were buying a concert ticket online. Some were told that a similar ticket had been sold to another customer for the same price; the others were told that another customer had gotten a better deal. Half the participants in each group interacted with a human ticket agent, while the other half interacted with a bot. Among those offered the similarly priced ticket, the type of agent made no difference to acceptance rates. But among participants offered the higher-priced ticket, just 19% of those interacting with a person wanted to buy it, while 49% of those interacting with a bot did. When the other customer was said to have paid a higher price, the opposite happened: The human agent (89%) than the bot (76%).

Later studies discovered why that pattern occurred. People thought bots were more fair with bad news (less selfish than humans) but less generous with good news (not as kind as humans). However, this difference became smaller when the bot had human features like a name or face.

“Our results reveal that an AI ‘bad guy’/human ‘good guy’ approach to managing disappointment should have beneficial results, when informing customers about unexpected delays or upgrades,” the researchers wrote. They add a warning: “In those cases where the worse-than-expected offer is objectively harmful to consumers, the use of this approach raises moral concerns.”
content: What does the underlined word “nuanced” in the first paragraph mean?
explanation: 词义猜测题。根据第一段“Research has shown that consumers often would rather interact with human agents... But a new study... When communicating a disappointing offer, a bot gets better results” 可知，新研究结果与以往不同，“nuanced” 意为“不同的” 。故选A。

subject: english
material:
Have you ever considered pairing up with a fitness friend? [[1]], but your physical performance through social interaction.

Exercise is contagious (传染的)

It’s no surprise to read that motivation is a benefit of working out with friends, but do you know exactly why this is? [[2]], according to a study published in the journal Nature Communications.

It boosts your workout frequency

[[3]]. People exercised more often when their friend offered emotional support and encouragement, over those offering just practical support. So, thank your workout buddy whenever they praise your effort, and do the same in return.

[[4]]

Endorphins (内啡肽) flood our system when we exercise, and this increases our tolerance to pain. People who exercise regularly can put up with physical discomfort for twice as long as those who don’t.

Having someone with you can also keep you safe. When strength training in the gym, having a trusted ‘spotter’ can ensure you lift safely. [[5]], particularly if it’s dark during winter months.
options: You feel less pain and stay safe
It’s also handy when out running
It enhances not just mental health
We all need cheerleaders on our fitness journey
Exercising with friends helps us achieve our goals
Apparently you can ‘catch’ a desire to exercise from other people
explanation: 上文提及找健身搭档这一话题，下文以“but” 引出社交互动对体能表现的益处。选项D“这不仅能改善心理健康” 中“not just” 与后文“but” 形成递进关系，补充了社交互动对心理健康的益处，符合语境。故选D。
