subject: english
content:
阅读短文，从方框中选择适当的词并用其正确形式填空，使短文通顺、意思完整。每空限填一词，每词限用一次。

think sometimes after give invite moment easy he with chance

How do you feel when you read a bad writing? Has a doctor ever [[36]] you a prescription (处方) to take to the chemist (药剂师) for some medicine? Are you able to read the prescription [[37]]? Some doctors write clearly but most doctors do not. Chemists have more [[38]] to read doctors’ notes. But [[39]] doctors write so badly that even the chemists can’t read them.

One day, a lady wrote to a doctor to [[40]] him to have dinner at her house. The doctor wrote an answer, but he didn’t write clearly and the lady couldn’t read it.

“What shall I do?” she said to her husband. “I don’t know whether he is coming or not. I don’t want to give him a telephone call and say I can’t read [[41]] writing.” Her husband [[42]] for a moment, and then he had an idea.

“Oh, dear, ” said his wife. “That’s a very good idea. ”

She went to the chemist’s shop and gave the doctor’s note to the chemist. [[43]] the chemist got the note, he read it very carefully. Then he said politely, “Could you wait a [[44]], madam?” He went to the back of the shop. After a few minutes he returned [[45]] a large bottle. He gave the bottle to the lady and said, “Three times a day and one spoonful at a time.”
explanation:
句意：医生是否曾经给你开过一张处方，让你去药剂师那里取药？根据“Has a doctor ever... you a prescription to take to the chemist for some medicine?”和备选词汇可知，此处表达医生是否曾经给过你处方，该句为现在完成时的一般疑问句，give“给予”符合句意，变为过去分词形式given。故填given。

句意：你能轻松地读懂处方吗？根据“Are you able to read the prescription...”和备选词汇可知，这里指轻松地读懂处方，easily是副词，修饰动词read，表示“轻松地、容易地”。故填easily。

句意：药剂师有更多机会阅读医生的笔记。根据“Chemists have more... to read doctors’ notes.”和备选词汇可知，此处表达有更多机会，chances“机会”符合句意，chance的复数形式。故填chances。

句意：但有时医生写得如此糟糕，以至于连药剂师都看不懂。根据“But... doctors write so badly that even the chemists can’t read them.”和备选词汇可知，此处表达有时医生写得如此糟糕，sometimes“有时”符合句意。故填sometimes。

句意：有一天，一位女士写信给一位医生，邀请他到她家吃晚饭。根据“One day, a lady wrote to a doctor to... him to have dinner at her house.”和备选词汇可知，此处表达邀请他到她家吃晚饭，invite“邀请”符合句意，用动词原形与空前to构成不定式。故填invite。

句意：我不想给他打电话说我看不懂他的字迹。根据“I don’t want to give him a telephone call and say I can’t read... writing.”和备选词汇可知，这里指看不懂他的字迹，his“他的”，形容词性物主代词，修饰名词writing。故填his。

句意：她丈夫想了一会儿，然后有了一个主意。根据“Her husband... for a moment, and then he had an idea.”和备选词汇可知，这里指想了一会儿，时态为一般过去时，thought“想、思考”，think的过去式，think for a while“想了一会”。故填thought。

句意：药剂师拿到处方后，他仔细地阅读了。根据“... the chemist got the note, he read it very carefully.”和备选词汇可知，此处表达时间上的先后，after“在……之后”符合句意，句首首字母大写。故填After。

句意：然后他礼貌地说：“夫人，您能稍等一下吗？”根据“Could you wait a..., madam?”和备选词汇可知，此处表达稍等一会，wait a moment“稍等”符合句意。故填moment。

句意：几分钟后，他拿着一个大瓶子回来了。根据“After a few minutes he returned... a large bottle.”和备选词汇可知，此处表达他拿着一个大瓶子回来了，with“带着、拿着”符合句意，表伴随。故填with。

subject: english
content:
阅读短文，根据语篇要求填空，使短文通顺、意思完整。每空限填一词。

As you walk in the city and look up, some skyscrapers (摩天大楼) may catch your eye. But [[46]] you ever heard of earthscrapers (摩地大楼)? Do you know what they look like?

Earthscrapers, as their name suggests, are the opposite of skyscrapers. So far, many architects (建筑师) have tried [[47]] build earthscrapers. The most famous one is an entry (参赛作品) designed by a company in Mexico. As shown in the picture, it [[48]]about 300 meters deep and includes a museum, a shopping mall, and ten floors of apartments. And the building would get natural light and fresh air through [[49]] central (中心的) hole. But many problems remain to be solved. So, there is still no such building.

Now, more and more people move to cities. So it might not take too long before these underground spaces are open to the public. Perhaps [[50]] the future, some of us may live and work hundreds of meters underground.
explanation:
句意：但是你听说过摩地大楼吗？根据“you ever heard of earthscrapers”可知此处表示过去的动作对现在的影响，用现在完成时，主语是you，助动词用have。故填have。

句意：到目前为止，许多建筑师都尽力建造摩地大楼。try to do sth.“尽力做某事”。故填to。

句意：如图所示，它大约有300米深，包括一个博物馆、一个购物中心和十层公寓。此处缺少be动词，句子用一般现在时，主语是it，be动词用is。故填is。

句意：而且，这座建筑可以通过一个中心孔获得自然光和新鲜空气。此处泛指“一个中心孔”，central以辅音音素开头，用不定冠词a。故填a。

句意：也许在未来的某一天，我们中的一些人可能会在地下几百米的地方生活和工作。in the future“在未来”。故填in。

subject: english
content:
根据下面的对话情景，在每个空白处填上一个适当的句子，使对话的意思连贯、完整。

A: Hi, Sarah! [[51]]?

B: Hi, John! I’m going to be a volunteer tour guide at the museum.

A: Great! It will be a meaningful experience.

B: That’s true. [[52]]?

A: Yes, I’d love to. And I just finished my volunteer work at the Community Library.

B: The Community Library? Sounds interesting. What did you do there?

A: [[53]]. It can be easier for people to find books they need.

B: What you did is really helpful. How often do you volunteer there?

A: [[54]].

B: Maybe we can do volunteer activities together next time. May I join you?

A: Sure! [[55]].

B: Thanks. I’m happy to be a member of your group, too.
answer: (1) What are you going to do/ What will you do today/...；(2) Would you like to join me/...；(3) I helped tidy up the books/I helped clear up the shelves/...；(4) Twice/Three times a week/...；(5) I’m glad you can join us/I’m excited that we can do volunteer work together/...
explanation:
根据“Hi, John! I’m going to be a volunteer tour guide at the museum.”可知此处应是询问对方去做什么，故填What are you going to do/ What will you do/...

根据“Yes, I’d love to.”可知此处是邀请对方一起，故填Would you like to join me/...

根据“What did you do there?”以及“It can be easier for people to find books they need.”可知此处应回应自己工作的内容是整理书籍，故填I helped tidy up the books/I helped clear up the shelves/...

根据“How often do you volunteer there?”可知应回应多久在那里做一次志愿者，故填Twice/Three times a week/...

根据“May I join you?”以及“Sure!”可知应是同意对方的加入，故填I’m glad you can join us/I’m excited that we can do volunteer work together/...

subject: english
content:
成长的道路上，我们努力改变以提升自我。学校英语广播站正在开展主题为“The Change Made Me Better”的征文活动，请你根据写作要求，用英语写一篇短文积极投稿。

写作要求：1. 文中须包含上图提示的所有信息，可适当发挥；

2. 文中不得出现考生的真实姓名和学校名称；

3. 词数100左右。

The Change Made Me Better
answer:
The Change Made Me Better

There are many things in my life that can help me to be better. For example, I used to be weak because of my bad living habits, but now I am stronger and healthier.

It was a terrible race that made me change. I fell down and was left behind by all the other students. This experience made me decide to change. I really wanted to keep up with others. So I started to exercise often and eat more healthily.

I realized that exercise and a healthy diet were the key to a good body. And this experience also made me strong-willed.

subject: english
content: Many old people are getting used to [[_]] with their phones.
explanation:
句意：许多老年人正在习惯用手机付款。

考查非谓语动词。pay付款（动词原形）；paying付款（动名词/现在分词）；paid付款（过去式/过去分词）。根据“getting used to”可知，此处是“get used to doing sth.”的固定搭配，意为“习惯做某事”，to是介词，后接动名词，用paying，故选B。

subject: english
content: Jill has [[_]] much homework [[_]] she can’t hang out with us.
explanation:
句意：吉尔有如此多的作业，以至于她不能和我们一起闲逛。

考查结果状语从句。too...to...太…… 而不能……，后接动词原形；such...that...如此……以至于……，修饰名词。“so...that...”意为“如此……以至于……”，可修饰形容词或副词，也可修饰“many/much/few/little（表数量）”。此处“much”表数量，用“so...that...”结构。故选C。

subject: english
content: Thanksgiving Day in the West is similar [[_]] the Mid-Autumn Festival in China.
explanation:
句意：西方的感恩节类似于中国的中秋节。

考查介词辨析。to到；as作为；with和。固定搭配be similar to，意为“与……相似”。故选A。

subject: english
content: The sign on the wall tells people [[_]] after drinking.
explanation:
句意：墙上的标志告诉人们酒后不要开车。

考查非谓语动词。根据语境可知，此处是告诉人们不要酒后开车，tell sb. not to do sth.表示“告诉某人不要做某事”，固定搭配，所以此处应该用not to drive。故选B。

subject: english
content: Please tell me [[_]] you will come to my party or not.
explanation:
句意：请告诉我你是否会来我的派对。

考查宾语从句引导词。when何时，用于询问时间；because因为，用于引导原因状语从句，不引导宾语从句；whether是否，可引导宾语从句。根据句末“or not”可知，此处需用“whether...or not”结构表“是否”，故选C。

subject: english
content:
—Could I play games with my friends this afternoon?

—Sure, you [[_]]. But you have to finish your homework first.
explanation:
句意：——今天下午我能和朋友们玩游戏吗？——当然可以。但你必须先完成作业。

考查情态动词辨析。could能，是can的过去式，也可用于委婉请求；can能，表许可或能力；can’t不能。问句用“Could I...”表委婉请求，答语“Sure”表同意许可，需用“can”回应。故选B。

subject: english
content: Your shoes are too dirty. They need [[_]].
explanation:
句意：你的鞋子太脏了。它们需要清洗。

考查非谓语动词。“need”后接非谓语动词时，有两种常见结构：“need doing sth”表示“某物需要被做”，主语通常是物；“need to do sth”表示“某人需要做某事”，主语通常是人。本句主语“They”指代“shoes”，需用“need washing”表示“鞋子需要被清洗”，故选A。

subject: english
content:
—Could you please tell me [[_]]?

—It’s about 30 dollars.
options: how much should I pay for it
how many I should pay for it
how much I should pay for it
explanation:
句意：——你能告诉我我应该付多少钱吗？——大约30美元。

考查宾语从句。宾语从句需用陈述语序，排除A项；“how many”后接可数名词复数，用于询问数量，“how much”可用于询问价格，后不接名词。根据答语“It’s about 30 dollars”可知，问句是对价格的提问，需用“how much”，且为陈述语序，排除B项。故选C。

subject: english
content:
—Excuse me, is there a post office near here?

—Yes, just go [[_]] the park and turn right at the second crossing.
explanation:
句意：——打扰一下，这附近有邮局吗？——是的，只要经过公园，然后在第二个十字路口向右拐。

考查介词的用法。pass通过（动词）；past经过（介词）；passed通过了（动词pass的过去式或过去分词）。此处需要介词表示“经过”，固定用法为“go past”。故选B。

subject: english
content: Teenagers should learn [[_]] to deal with their stress.
explanation:
句意：青少年应该学会如何处理他们的压力。

考查疑问词加不定式结构。who谁；what什么；how如何。根据语境可知，此处是在说青少年应该学会“如何”处理压力，所以应该用how，表示方式。结合“疑问词+不定式”结构，此处应用how to deal with their stress表示“如何处理他们的压力”。故选C。

subject: english
content: Tony has made many friends [[_]] he came to our school.
explanation:
句意：托尼自从来到我们学校以来，已经交了很多朋友。

考查连词辨析。since自从；for为了；when当……时候。根据“Tony has made many friends”可知，主句是现在完成时，所以应该用since引导时间状语从句，表示“自从……以来”，与现在完成时连用。for后接一段时间，不可引导从句；when引导时间状语从句时，主句一般不用现在完成时。故选A。

subject: english
content:
—Which boy do you think [[_]] the most pounds during the vacation?

—Marcus, I think.
explanation:
句意：——你认为哪个男孩在假期期间体重增加最多？——我觉得是马库斯。

考查动词短语。put on增加（体重、衣物等）；turned on打开（电器等）；got on上车、进展。结合宾语“the most pounds”，“put on”可搭配“pounds”表示“增重”，符合语境。故选A。

subject: english
content: Teenagers are [[_]] tired because they have [[_]] homework to do every day.
explanation:
句意：青少年太累了，因为他们每天有太多作业要做。

考查短语辨析。“much too”修饰形容词或副词，意为“太……”；“too much”修饰不可数名词，意为“太多……”；“too many”修饰可数名词复数。第一空“tired”是形容词，用“much too”；第二空“homework”是不可数名词，用“too much”。故选A。

subject: english
content: He [[_]] goes to school by taxi because it’s too expensive.
explanation:
句意：他很少坐出租车去学校，因为它太贵了。

考查副词辨析。often经常；seldom很少；sometimes有时；根据原因“because it’s too expensive”可知，费用太贵，应是很少坐出租车去学校，B项符合，故选B。

subject: english
content: We have to face the difficulties [[_]] when we grow up.
explanation:
句意：我们长大后必须亲自面对困难。

考查介词短语。in person亲自；in public在公共场合；in need在危难中。结合“face the difficulties”和“when we grow up”的语境可知，长大后面对困难需要“亲自”去应对，符合逻辑。故选A。

subject: english
content: I like reading books made [[_]] paper, not on screens.
explanation:
句意：我喜欢阅读用纸制成的书，而不是屏幕上的。

考查短语介词搭配。be made of由……制成（能看出原材料）；be made into被制成……；be made from由……制成（看不出原材料）。书由纸制成，能看出原材料。故选A。

subject: english
content: He loves reading. Most of his money [[_]] on books.
explanation:
句意：他喜欢读书。他的大部分钱都花在买书上。

考查一般现在时的被动语态。句子主语“Most of his money”是动作“spend”的承受者，二者存在被动关系，需用被动语态；且描述的是常态情况，用一般现在时，因此填is spent。故选C。

subject: english
content: As we all know, China is well-known [[_]] tea.
explanation:
句意：众所周知，中国因茶而著名。

考查介词辨析和形容词短语。for因为；as作为；of……的。“be well-known for”意为“因……而闻名”；“be well-known as”意为“作为……而闻名”。此处表示中国因茶而著名，强调原因。故选A。

subject: english
content: People can hardly avoid [[_]] products made in China.
explanation:
句意：人们几乎无法避免购买中国制造的产品。

考查非谓语。avoid doing sth.“避免做某事”，为固定搭配，此处应用动名词buying。故选A。

subject: english
content: They found [[_]] difficult to work out the problem without any help.
explanation:
句意：他们发现在没有任何帮助的情况下解决这个问题是困难的。

考查it作形式宾语。根据“They found...difficult to work out”可知，此处考查“find it+ 形容词+ to do sth.”是固定结构。it作形式宾语，真正的宾语是后面的不定式短语；this和that无此用法。故选B。

subject: english
material:
I [[21]] in the UK last weekend to learn English. So far I have already made [[22]] friends and had some traditional English food there. But [[23]] having hamburgers, sandwiches and potatoes, I thought none could be [[24]] than Chinese food, [[25]] my favorite—huo guo. You can’t imagine how [[26]] I was when I got to know that there was going to [[27]] a free meal of hotpot to welcome the new students. On the way to the canteen, I seemed to smell huo guo in the air.

To my [[28]], when I stepped into the room, I didn’t see any sign of huo guo. Where was it?

[[29]] many questions in my head, I [[30]] down to have the free meal. After I talked with an English girl, I got to know that Chinese huo guo was completely different [[31]] hotpot. Chinese huo guo is [[32]] in two words—hot pot; and hotpot, one word, is a traditional English dish.

Hotpot is made from mutton and onion. On the top are pieces of potatoes. People put it in the oven all day in a heavy pot on a low heat. It [[33]] very little effort to prepare. You can often see it at parties in the UK because it’s easy [[34]] for many people and is not expensive.

Hotpot tastes [[35]]. However, I still miss huo guo—hot pot, two words!

句意：我上周末到达英国学习英语。

arrived到达，后加介词in/at；reached到达，后加地点；got表示“到达”时，后加to。根据“in the UK”可知此处用arrived。故选A。

subject: english
content:
用所给单词的适当形式填空，完成短文。

If you spend some time [[36]] (live) in an English-speaking country, you might hear the word “etiquette”. It [[37]] (mean) normal and polite social behavior. Etiquette is not the same in different cultures. For example, standing very close to the person you are talking with is quite common in some [[38]] (Asia) countries. However, if you do this in Europe, some people might feel [[39]] (comfortable). Perhaps we think that talking [[40]] (loud) in our own home is fine, but in other places it is not [[41]] (allow). For example, most people would agree that talking in a high voice in a library, a museum or a movie theater is [[42]] (polite). Even if you are with your friends, it is better [[43]] (keep) your voice down in public places. If we see someone break the rules of etiquette, we may politely give them some [[44]] (advice). You can ask them politely “Would you mind not doing this?” Of course, people don’t usually like to be criticized (批评), so we have to be [[45]] (care) how we do this.
answer: (1) living；(2) means；(3) Asian；(4) uncomfortable；(5) loudly；(6) allowed；(7) impolite；(8) to keep；(9) advice；(10) careful
explanation:
句意：如果你花些时间在说英语的国家生活，你可能会听到“礼仪”这个词。“spend time doing sth.”是固定用法，需用动词-ing形式，“live”的-ing形式是“living”。故填living。

句意：它意思是正常且礼貌的社会行为。主语“It”是第三人称单数，谓语动词用第三人称单数形式，“mean”的第三人称单数是“means”。故填means。

句意：例如，在一些亚洲国家，和你交谈的人站得很近是很常见的。修饰名词“countries”需用形容词，“Asia”的形容词形式是“Asian”。故填Asian。

句意：然而，如果你在欧洲这样做，有些人可能会感到不舒服。根据语境，此处表示“不舒服的”，“comfortable”的否定形式是“uncomfortable”。故填uncomfortable。

句意：也许我们认为在自己家里大声说话是可以的，但在其他地方是不被允许的。修饰动词“talking”需用副词，“loud”的副词形式是“loudly”。故填loudly。

句意：也许我们认为在自己家里大声说话是可以的，但在其他地方是不被允许的。“it”与“allow”是被动关系，“be+过去分词”构成被动语态，allow的过去分词是“allowed”。故填allowed。

句意：例如，大多数人会同意在图书馆、博物馆或电影院大声说话是不礼貌的。根据语境，此处表示“不礼貌的”，“polite”的否定形式是“impolite”。故填impolite。

句意：即使你和朋友在一起，在公共场所最好压低你的声音。“it is better to do sth.”是固定句型，需用不定式“to do”。故填to keep。

句意：如果我们看到有人违反礼仪规则，我们可以礼貌地给他们一些建议。“advice”是不可数名词，没有复数形式。故填advice。

句意：当然，人们通常不喜欢被批评，所以我们必须小心我们如何做这件事。“be”后需接形容词作表语，“care”的形容词形式是“careful”。故填careful。

subject: english
content:
用适当的词语或句子补全对话。

A: Good morning, Wu Lei! [[51]]?

B: Hi, Dave. My favorite festival is the Mid-Autumn Festival.

A: [[52]] Chang’e?

B: Of course. It’s a traditional folk story.

A: [[53]]?

B: Sure. Chang’e was Hou Yi’s wife. She took magic medicine and flew up to the moon and couldn’t come back.

A: Did Hou Yi miss his wife?

B: [[54]]. He wished that his wife could return. He often laid out food in memory of his wife when the moon became round. Later, people started the tradition of admiring the moon and sharing mooncakes with their families.

A: I see. I also like the Mid-Autumn Festival. I think it’s very important to spend time with our families.

B: Yes, [[55]].
answer: (1) What’s your favorite festival；(2) Do you know the story of；(3) Can you tell me something about it；(4) Yes, he did；(5) I think so/I agree
explanation:
根据“B: Hi, Dave. My favorite festival is the Mid-Autumn Festival.”可知，B回答“我最喜欢的节日是中秋节”，由此可推测A的问题是“你最喜欢的节日是什么”，故填What’s your favorite festival。

根据“B: Of course. It’s a traditional folk story.”以及后文提及嫦娥奔月的故事可知，A的问题是“你知道嫦娥的故事吗”，故填Do you know the story of。

根据“B: Sure. Chang’e was Hou Yi’s wife. She took magic medicine and flew up to the moon and couldn’t come back.”可知，B详细讲述了嫦娥的故事，由此可推测A的问题是“你能给我讲讲它（嫦娥的故事）吗”，“Sure”表明此处是请求对方讲述故事，故填Can you tell me something about it。

根据“A: Did Hou Yi miss his wife?”以及“B: ... He wished that his wife could return. He often laid out food in memory of his wife”可知，后羿思念妻子，此处应作肯定回答，问句是一般过去时的一般疑问句，回答需保持时态一致，故填Yes, he did。

根据“A: I think it’s very important to spend time with our families. B: Yes, ...”可知，B认同A“与家人共度时光很重要”的观点，此处应表达“我也这么认为/我同意”，故填I think so/I agree。

The Dragon Boat Festival, also called the Duanwu Festival, is celebrated on the fifth day of the fifth month according to the Chinese calendar.

For thousands of years, the festival has been marked by eating zongzi and racing dragon boats. [[56]]

[[57]] He was an honest minister (大臣) of the Chu State, during the Warring States Period (475 B.C. to 221 B.C.).

He was kind and wise. He wanted to bring his country peace and make the state much stronger, but he failed. [[58]] He ended his life by throwing himself into the Miluo River. It was said that people jumped from boats into the river and tried to save him, but it was too late. [[59]]

Now on the Dragon Boat Festival we read Qu Yuan’s poem “Li Sao” and remember his deep love for his motherland. [[60]].

Marie is a famous woman in the world. She made a lot of important contributions (贡献) to the development of humans. She was born in Poland in 1867. Her father worked as a middle school headmaster and taught math and physics, so she enjoyed and did well in these two subjects at school. Marie went to study in University of Paris in 1891. The Spring Festival is celebrated not only in China but also in other parts of the world. The traditional holiday is the most important to Chinese both at home and abroad.

The United Kingdom

Celebrations for the Spring Festival in the UK started in 1980, with the first evening party held in 2002. Every New Year, people get together and have a lot of activities. They sing songs, dance to music, share photos with friends or enjoy films in the cinema.

The United States

This Spring Festival has become a key time for Chinese living or working in the US. They join in a large evening party to welcome the traditional New Year. It is a good chance for people to build a circle of friends and feel that they are not alone because they share the same culture and values.

Australia

The Chinese New Year will be welcomed with three weeks of celebrations across Australia. Many people come to Sydney’s Chinatown or Little Bourke in Melbourne. They enjoy fireworks, lion dances and dragon boat races. The celebrations are also a bridge towards better understanding between Chinese and non-Chinese.

Singapore

The family dinner on New Year’s Eve is an important tradition for Chinese whether they were born in Singapore or moved there from China. They place traditional food on a table as an act of remembering their past. Then the whole family enjoy their dinner together. They usually hold it at home because having it in a restaurant takes away the meaning of the tradition.

A father bought a kite for his son. The son couldn’t wait to fly it. So, on the next windy day, they took the kite to a park.

First, the father taught his son to fly the kite. Soon, the son was flying the kite high in the air. When it couldn’t go higher, the son realized something. “The string (线) is holding the kite down,” he said to himself. “If I cut it, it can fly higher.”

The son cut the string. After that, the kite flew up a little more. However, the kite didn’t rise for long. It slowly came down until it landed in a tree far away. The son was surprised. “I thought the kite could fly higher without the string,” he said. “What happened?”

“The string wasn’t holding the kite down,” said the father. “It was helping it stay higher. After you cut the string, the string couldn’t support (支持) the kite.”

Really, rules are like the string that seems to hold us down in our daily lives. But, without them, we can’t fly high like the kite. We should never let go of them.

explanation: 根据文章第1段“they took the kite to a park”可知，他们在公园放风筝。故填He flew the kite in a park./In a park.

answer: （1）Listen and speak as much as you can. Try to practice English every day by listening to songs or talking with friends. （2）Read English stories. It’s a fun way to improve your listening and learn daily expressions. （5）Don’t be afraid of making mistakes. Just try your best to use English, and you will make progress.

content: 假如你校要组织一次英语演讲比赛，请你以“Changes in My Hometown”为题，从人们的住房、环境、交通等方面进行今昔对比，写一篇英语短文参赛。
answer:
Changes in My Hometown

Hi, everybody,

I believe my hometown will get better and better in the future.

subject: english
material:
On the morning of 3 April, 2024, a 7.3-magnitude earthquake (7.3级地震) hit the sea area near Hualien. As of 8 April, the earthquake had killed 13 people and hurt more than 1,140. There had been more than 20 aftershocks (余震) of magnitude 5 or above in Hualien, as of 10 April.

What to do during an earthquake

Inside: Don’t stand in a doorway. You are safer under a table.

Outside: Move away from buildings, trees, and gas lines.

In a crowded place: Drop down onto the floor, cover your head and neck, and hold on to something safe.

In a theatre: Stay in your seat. Protect your head and neck with your arms or any way possible.

Earthquake warning

People may get warnings of an earthquake before it arrives. How does this work? There are many seismometers (地震监测波) in different areas. When the earth starts shaking, the machines quickly tell how strong it is and then send a warning before the earthquake waves arrive in other areas further away.
content: What should you do when you are outside during an earthquake?
explanation: 细节理解题。根据“What to do during an earthquake”部分中“Outside: Move away from buildings, trees, and gas lines.”可知，地震时在室外应远离建筑物。故选D。

subject: english
material:
(After listening to Mr. Jason’s advice, Andrew decided to try to improve his relationship with his mother.)

There were some problems between my mother and me. In the past, she always asked me to be good at everything. I felt very tired of that.

But when I started to share my ideas with her, things changed. I realised that the reason for her pushing (推动) me was that she wanted me to be able to take good care of myself in the future. I also told her that I needed more rest. Finally, we found the best way to solve this problem—to reduce some of my activities. As our relationship improved, my mother became more like a friend to me. When she was tired after working for a long time, I always told her some interesting things that happened at school to make her happy.

My mother encouraged me a lot whenever I faced problems. Last month, I was seriously ill and couldn’t go to school. My grades dropped a lot. However, my mother didn’t blame (责怪) me but helped me with my studies. To improve my grades, I studied until late at night. My mother always stayed with me in my room. It warmed my heart.

Luckily, my grades improved a lot. After the tests, I used my pocket money to buy a cake for her. The good grades were not only mine but also hers. Now I have realised how important communication is. If we stop arguing and start communicating with others, we will make a difference in our lives.
content: What was the best way to solve the problem between Andrew and his mother?
options: To take a trip to a new place.
To have a delicious dinner together.
To reduce some of Andrew’s activities.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据“Finally, we found the best way to solve this problem—to reduce some of my activities.”可知，解决Andrew和母亲之间问题的最佳方式是减少Andrew的一些活动。故选D。

options: Because he argued with his mother.
Because he went out and had fun.
Because he didn’t listen carefully in class.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据“Last month, I was seriously ill and couldn’t go to school. My grades dropped a lot.”可知，Andrew成绩下降是因为他生病了无法上学。故选B。

subject: english
material:
Curiosity is like a spark (火花) that can start a fire of invention. It plays a very important role in the world of invention.

When inventors are curious, they look at things in new ways. They wonder why things work the way they do and how they can be made better. For example, Thomas Edison was curious about light. He asked questions like “Why can’t we make a room brighter in a better way?” This curiosity led him to invent the light bulb. Without curiosity, many of the amazing inventions we use today might not exist (存在).

We can do something to cultivate curiosity. First, we should ask a lot of questions. When we see something new or strange, we can ask “What is it?” “How does it work?” and “Why is it like this?” Don’t be afraid of looking silly. Any question can be a step towards discovery.

Second, we can explore new places. A trip to a science museum or a nature park can open our eyes to new things. We might see strange animals or cool scientific displays that make us want to learn more.

Third, we can try new hobbies. Whether it’s building model planes or growing plants, new hobbies can make us curious about different fields.
content: How does the writer develop his idea in Paragraph 2?
explanation: 细节理解题。根据“For example, Thomas Edison was curious about light. He asked questions like ‘Why can’t we make a room brighter in a better way?’ This curiosity led him to invent the light bulb.”可知，作者在第二段通过列举爱迪生因对光好奇而发明电灯泡的例子来阐述观点，所以是通过举例的方式展开观点的。故选C。

subject: english
material:
Sometimes the world may feel like an unhappy place. However, you can make a difference. If you make even a person smile today, you can help make this world a better place. Here is a list of ideas to help you.

Send a handwritten letter. In this age where everything is sent by email, it is a surprise to receive a letter through the post. Writing a few words on paper to a friend is an easy way to make one smile. Even a postcard with a couple of sentences could really make someone’s day—all for the price of a stamp.

Volunteer. Volunteering is one of the nicest things you can do. It needs some time and research to find the perfect project before volunteering. There are so many chances, so you are sure to find one that is right for you. And it doesn’t necessarily have to take up all your time—it could be once a week or a couple of times a year.

Make something for a special person. Whether you’re creative or not, taking time to make something for someone else shows how thankful you are to him or her. Even if you think you are not creative, the receiver will feel lucky to get such a special gift that you put your time into. Some ideas could include a card, a painting, a song, a poem or a cake!

Tell someone “I love you”. It can be a family member or a friend. Perhaps you can tell a friend that you appreciate all he or she does for you, or tell your mum that you love her. Sometimes, in our busy lives, we forget to take a moment to tell people what they mean to us.
content: How do we feel if we get a letter through the post?
answer: We feel surprised./It is a surprise to receive a letter through the post.
explanation: 根据原文第一段“In this age where everything is sent by email, it is a surprise to receive a letter through the post.”可知在如今电子邮件普及的时代，收到一封邮寄来的信会让人感到惊喜。直接提取原文的核心信息“surprised”。故填We feel surprised. /It is a surprise to receive a letter through the post.

subject: english
content:
阅读短文内容，在空白处填入一个适当的单词或括号内单词的正确形式。

Anna is a UK exchange student in China. She [[31]] (be) back in the UK for three days to spend the Christmas holiday with her family. She enjoys Christmas and the delicious food, but she has had some digital problems there.

Today, she decided to ride a shared bike to a shop to get some vegetables and meat. But it took her forever [[32]] (find) a bike! She finally found an old one. But that 20-minute ride [[33]] (cost) her an arm and a leg—more than four pounds!

Then after getting everything she needed in the shop, she wanted to pay [[34]] her smartphone. She asked the shopkeeper to show the QR code, but the shopkeeper didn’t understand! Next, she tried to use her digital wallet, but the shop’s [[35]] (pay) system didn’t work. The shopkeeper told her [[36]] (use) cash. She had to go home to get some cash because she didn’t carry her wallet. She has been used to digital payments in China.

Finally, she got home. She was so tired that she gave up on [[37]] (cook). She ordered her favourite dishes through [[38]] app instead, but the delivery was really slow. When her dishes finally arrived 90 minutes later, they were stone-cold! By then, she felt tired and hungry. For Anna, she has had a great holiday except for today. Thinking of the [[39]] (convenient) of digital life, she is [[40]] (look) forward to going back to China.
explanation: 31.句意：她已经回英国三天了，要和家人一起过圣诞假期。根据“for three days”可知，此处用现在完成时，主语“She”是第三人称单数，结构为“has been”。故填has been。32.句意：但找一辆单车花了她很长时间！根据“But it took her forever…a bike!”可知，“it takes/took sb.+一段时间+to do sth.”是固定结构，表示“做某事花费某人多少时间”，it作形式主语，空处使用动词不定式作真正的主语。故填to find。33.句意：但20分钟的骑行花了她一大笔钱——超过4英镑！根据“She finally found an old one.”可知，时态为一般过去时，动词使用过去式，“cost”的过去式为“cost”。故填cost。34.句意：然后在商店买完需要的东西后，她想用智能手机付款。根据“pay…her smartphone”可知，此处表示“用（工具）”，用介词“with”。故填with。35.句意：接下来，她尝试使用数字钱包，但商店的支付系统坏了。根据“the shop’s…system”可知，此处修饰名词“system”，要用“pay”的名词形式“payment”。故填payment。36.句意：店主告诉她用现金支付。根据“told her”可知，“tell sb. to do sth.”是固定搭配，意为“告诉某人做某事”，空处使用动词不定式。故填to use。37.句意：她太累了，所以放弃了做饭。根据“she gave up on”可知，on是介词，后接名词、代词或动名词，“give up on doing sth.”是固定搭配，意为“放弃做某事”。故填cooking。38.句意：她通过一个应用点了最喜欢的菜，但配送太慢了。 根据“…app”可知，“app”是单数名词，此处表泛指“一个”，且“app”以元音音素开头，用不定冠词“an”。故填an。39.句意：想到数字生活的便利，她盼望着回到中国。根据“the…of digital life”可知，空处使用名词，“convenient”要变为名词形式“convenience”，表示“数字生活的便利”。故填convenience。40.句意：想到数字生活的便利，她盼望着回到中国。根据“is…forward to”可知，此处是现在进行时，“look”的现在分词是“looking”。故填looking。

subject: english
content:
阅读短文，从方框中选择适当的词或词组并用其正确形式填空，使短文通顺，意思完整。(每词或词组限用一次。)

in real life wise although be good for spend much time

We believe that digital life [[41]] us. It makes life easier and more fun. Digital technology helps us stay connected with friends and family through video calls and messages. It is also great for learning because we can find information online and watch videos to understand new things. However, [[42]] on screens can hurt our eyes and make us tired. People often forget to spend time with family and friends [[43]] because they are busy with phones or computers. For example, kids may stop playing outside and become less active. [[44]] digital technology is useful, we must be careful not to let it take up all our time. We should use digital technology [[45]] and safely.
answer: (1) is good for；(2) spending much time；(3) in real life；(4) Although；(5) wisely
explanation: 41.句意：我们认为数字生活对我们有益。它让生活更便捷、更有趣。根据“It makes life easier and more fun.”可知，此处表达“数字生活对我们有益”。be good for意为“对……有益”，主语“digital life”是单数，时态是一般现在时，故be动词用is。故填is good for 。42.句意：然而，花很多时间在屏幕上会伤害我们的眼睛，还会让我们疲惫。根据“hurt our eyes and make us tired”可知，此处是说“长时间看屏幕”的行为。spend much time意为“花很多时间”，句子缺主语，动词短语作主语时，动词用动名词形式，因此spend变为spending。故填spending much time。43.句意：人们常常因为忙着玩手机或电脑，忘记了在现实生活中陪伴家人和朋友。根据“because they are busy with phones or computers”可知，此处是对比“线上”和“现实生活”的陪伴。介词短语“in real life”作状语，修饰动词短语“spend time with...”，符合语境。故填in real life。44.句意：虽然数字技术很有用，但我们必须注意不要让它占据我们所有的时间。根据“useful和“not to let it take up all our time”的转折关系可知，此处需要转折连词。连词although引导让步状语从句，表“虽然；尽管”，符合逻辑，位于句首，首字母要大写。故填Although。45.句意：我们应该明智地、安全地使用数字技术。根据“and safely”可知，此处需要一个副词和safely并列，修饰动词use。形容词“wise”的副词形式是“wisely”，表示“明智地”。故填wisely。

subject: english
content:
Kitty and her parents lived in Beijing two years ago. (用for two years改写句子)

Kitty and her parents [[_]] [[_]] in Beijing for two years.
explanation: 句意：Kitty和她的父母两年前住在北京。“for two years”是现在完成时的时间标志，现在完成时结构为“have/has + 过去分词”，主语“Kitty and her parents”是复数，助动词用have；“live”的过去分词是lived。故填have；lived。

subject: english
content:
Jack has made progress in English since he studied online. (对划线部分提问)

[[_]] [[_]] has Jack made progress in English?
explanation: 句意：Jack自从在网上学习后，英语取得了进步。划线部分表示时间段，应用特殊疑问词组how long提问，故填How；long。

subject: english
content:
Many travellers sang along with the music of “My Motherland and I” yesterday.（用at this time yesterday改写句子）

Many travellers [[_]] [[_]] along with the music of “My Motherland and I” at this time yesterday.
explanation: 句意：许多游客昨天跟着《我和我的祖国》的音乐一起唱。 用“at this time yesterday”改写后，需体现“过去某个具体时间正在进行的动作”，要用过去进行时，结构：was/were + 动词现在分词。 主语“Many travellers”是复数，be动词用“were”； “sing”的现在分词是“singing”。故填were；singing。

subject: english
content:
That night, I slept at home. (用when the ground shook very hard改写句子)

That night, I [[_]] [[_]] at home when the ground shook very hard.
explanation: 句意：那天晚上，当地面剧烈摇晃时，我正在家里睡觉。when引导时间状语从句，强调“地面剧烈摇晃”这个短暂动作发生时，“我在家睡觉”这个持续动作正在进行。根据过去进行时的用法，结构为was/were+现在分词，主语为I，对应的be动词过去式是was，sleep的现在分词形式是sleeping。故填was；sleeping。

subject: english
content:
We should wear seat belts in cars to stay safe on the road. (改为同义句)

We should wear seat belts in cars [[_]] [[_]] to stay safe on the road.
explanation: 句意：我们在汽车里应该系好安全带，以在道路上保持安全。原句“to stay safe on the road”在句中作目的状语，表示为了在道路上保持安全，等同于in order to/so as to“为了”。故填in/so；order/as。

subject: english
content:
Smartphones are useful, but we shouldn’t let them take up all our time.（英译汉）

[[_]]
answer: 智能手机很有用，但是我们不应该让它们占据了我们所有的时间。
explanation: “Smartphones are useful”翻译为“智能手机很有用”；“but”翻译为“但是”，连词，表转折；“we shouldn’t”翻译为“我们不应该”； “let them”翻译为“让它们”； “take up”翻译为“占据（了），占用”； “all our time”翻译为“我们所有的时间”。故填：智能手机很有用，但是我们不应该让它们占据了我们所有的时间。

subject: english
content:
Rules aren’t just on the wall but also in our minds and hearts. (英译汉)

[[_]]
answer: 规则不仅仅在墙上，也在我们的思想和心里。
explanation: 句中Rules是主语，意为“规则”；aren’t是系动词的否定形式，表示“不是”；not just...but also...是固定搭配，意为“不仅……而且……”；on the wall是介词短语作表语，意为“在墙上”；in our minds and hearts是介词短语作表语，意为“在我们的思想和心里”。故填：规则不仅仅在墙上，也在我们的思想和心里。

subject: english
content:
记住网上的不良行为是有代价的。（汉译英）

[[_]]
answer: Remember that bad behavior online has costs.
explanation: 记住：remember；网上的不良行为：bad behavior online；是有代价的：have costs。结合语境可知，此处使用包含宾语从句的祈使句，用于提出建议，以动词原形remember开头，后接that引导的宾语从句，bad behavior online作从句主语，从句时态为一般现在时，从句谓语动词have使用第三人称单数形式has。故填Remember that bad behavior online has costs.

subject: english
content:
只要你努力并坚持你的梦想，没有什么是不可能的。（汉译英）

[[_]]
answer: As long as you work hard and stick to your dreams, nothing is impossible.
explanation: “只要”翻译为as long as；“你”翻译为you；“努力”翻译为work hard；“并”翻译为and；“坚持你的梦想”翻译为stick to your dreams；“没有什么是不可能的”翻译为nothing is impossible。故填As long as you work hard and stick to your dreams, nothing is impossible.

subject: english
content:
我们应该勇敢地面对伤口和疼痛。（汉译英）

[[_]]
answer: We should face wounds and pain bravely.
explanation: 我们：we，位于句首，首字母大写；应该：should，后跟动词原形；面对：face；伤口：wound，名词用复数表示泛指；和：and；疼痛：pain，不可数名词；勇敢地：bravely。故填We should face wounds and pain bravely.

subject: english
content:
为了管理好班级，给大家营造良好的学习环境，班主任让每位同学制定班规。请你结合下图，制定一些合理的班级制度并给出每一条规则的理由。

Class rules

What the rules are

Listen carefully in class.

Don’t run or fight in the classroom.

...

...

Why they are important

This rule is useful because...

In my opinion, we follow the rule in order to...

...

...

要求：（1）短文须包含上图所有要点，并补充两点规则和理由；（2）可适当增加细节，以使行文连贯；（3）文中不得出现真实姓名及学校名称；（4）词数为70词左右。开头和结尾已给出，不计入总词数。

Class Rules

To make our class better, we need to make some rules. Please follow them.

____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

If we don’t break any of them, our class will be better.
answer:
范文：

Class Rules

To make our class better, we need to make some rules. Please follow them.

First, listen carefully in class. This rule is important because it helps us learn better. Second, don’t run or fight in the classroom. It keeps us safe and the class tidy. Third, finish homework on time. It helps review what we learned. Fourth, be polite to others. It makes our class friendly.

In my opinion, we follow these rules in order to have a good learning environment. If we don’t break any of them, our class will be better.

material:
(B)

The Internet, mobile phones and AI are parts of our lives now. Technology is greatly affecting (影响) many ways of our lives, from the ways we work to the ways we play. There is no doubt that humans will continue to use more and more technology. Here are some examples of modern technology that will change our ideas and will affect our lives greatly.

Global Positioning System (GPS)

It’s a system. The system uses radio signals (信号) from satellites to show exact information. It tells you where the user is on the earth in all weather conditions. It’s made up of three parts: satellites, control equipment (设备) on land and receivers.

Space Technology

Russian and American scientists have worked together for the International Space Station (ISS) for a long time. They hope the ISS will provide a long-lasting lab. Such a lab will bring humans endless advantages (优势). It’s even hoped that one day space technology will take humans to their new houses in space.

Underwater Robot

Hercules is a kind of underwater robot with some high technology equipment. It will be used to search for ancient ships. These ships sank into the deep sea during their journey long ago.

The world is changing so quickly that it’s hard for us to catch up with all the new inventions because they seem to come out every month. It’s important for us to learn about new technology and the role that it plays in our lives. So we should be willing to accept modern technology, or we will fall behind the times.

subject: english
material:
(C)

When you are in a new place in English-speaking countries, it’s important and necessary to know how to ask for directions. It can help you get to your destination (目的地) faster and avoid getting lost.

The first and most important step is to start the conversation politely. When you ask for directions, the way you make your request can make a difference to the reply you receive. Using polite expressions shows respect for the person you’re asking. This makes him/her more likely to help you. If possible, put on a smile.

Once you’ve started the conversation, you’d better ask for directions by using simple sentences. Here are some English expressions for you to ask for directions. Combining them with a friendly attitude (态度) will increase your chances of receiving helpful directions.

 Could you please tell me the way to the bookshop?

 Excuse me, can you give me directions to this house?

 I’m sorry to trouble you, but what’s the best way to reach Donald Street?

When you receive directions, it’s important to make sure that you’ve understood them correctly. You can repeat what the person has said, ask him to repeat certain details (细节) or ask for further explanation. This not only shows that you’ve been listening carefully but also provides a chance to correct any misunderstandings. Here are some expressions to help you, too.

 Let me make sure I understood correctly. I should turn left, is that right?

 Did you say I need to turn left at the central park?

 Would it be possible for you to write down the directions for me?

Finally, when you have the information you need, don’t forget to thank the person for his/her help.

根据语篇内容选择最佳答案。

explanation: 细节理解题。根据“Using polite expressions shows respect for the person you’re asking. This makes him/her more likely to help you.”可知，作者认为问路时礼貌是很重要的。故选B。

subject: english
material:
Chikungunya is an illness spread by tiger mosquitoes (虎蚊). These mosquitoes move around during the day most often about 6 to 8 in the morning and 5 to 7 in the afternoon. subject: english
content:
从方框中选择适当的词填空，使短文意思完整。每空限填一词，每词限用一次。方框中有一个词为多余项

relatives habit skills tradition produced importance encouraged express remain

Chinese New Year begins with doors and walls. Spring couplets stand for people’s wishes for a happier life in the coming year. The [[36]] of sticking spring couplets can date back (追溯) hundreds of years. The couplets are written on red paper. They hold great [[37]] during the Spring Festival. People are busy with all kinds of things before the Spring Festival, but sticking couplets is always in the first place on the to-do list. During my childhood my parents [[38]] me to learn how to write couplets. I asked elder people to teach me some [[39]]. When learning from them, I became greatly interested in traditional culture. Every time when our family visited [[40]] during the Spring Festival, I always collected the poems of their couplets. The poems are hopeful words. They [[41]] good wishes like “health, wealth and longevity (长寿).” Nowadays couplets are mainly [[42]] by machines. We can easily buy all kinds of beautiful couplets on the streets. Ways of making couplets have changed, yet the best wishes carried by couplets [[43]]. The red paper and black words are not only used to write the couplets, but also carry our love for traditional culture. They will never be forgotten.
explanation:
句意：贴春联的习俗可以追溯到几百年前。根据“The...of sticking spring couplets”可知，此处指的是贴春联的传统，应用名词tradition“传统”。故填tradition。

句意：它们在春节期间有着重要的意义。根据“They hold great...during the Spring Festival.”可知，春联在春节期间有重要的意义，应用名词importance“重要性”。故填importance。

句意：在我童年时期，我的父母鼓励我学习如何写春联。根据“me to learn how to write couplets”可知，此处是encourage sb to do sth“鼓励某人做某事”，句子是过去时，动词用过去式。故填encouraged。

句意：我请长辈教我一些技巧。根据“I asked elder people to teach me some...”可知，此处指的是学习写春联的“技巧”应用名词skills“技巧”。故填skills。

句意：每年春节我们全家拜访亲戚的时候，我总是收集他们的对联诗。根据“our family visited...”可知，此处指的是拜访亲戚，应用名词relatives“亲戚”。故填relatives。

句意：它们表达了诸如“健康、财富和长寿”之类的美好祝愿。根据“good wishes”可知，此处指的是表达美好的祝愿，应用动词express“表达”，句子是一般现在时，主语是复数，动词用原形。故填express。

句意：如今，春联主要是由机器生产的。根据“couplets are mainly...by machines”可知，此处指的是春联被机器生产，应用动词produced“生产”，此处是被动结构，动词用过去分词。故填produced。

句意：贴春联的方式已经改变了，但春联所承载的美好祝愿依然存在。根据“yet the best wishes carried by couplets...”可知，此处指的是美好的祝愿依然存在，应用动词remain“保持，依然”，句子是一般现在时，主语是复数，动词用原形。故填remain。

subject: english
content:
根据语篇内容填写所缺单词或用所给单词的正确形式填空，使语篇意思完整。

At the 2024 Paris Olympic Games, Ma Long extended (拓展) his record to six Olympic gold medals. Ma Long is widely regarded as one of the greatest [[44]] (play) in the history of table tennis.

He has been enjoying playing table tennis since he [[45]] a child. Ma got his first world championship at the age of 18, but he knew it was not enough. He wanted to win more championships. However, he missed the finals in the next few years, which gave him too much pressure. [[46]] he failed many times, he kept on training day after day. He didn’t want to give [[47]] his dream. And the coach told him that the only one who can beat him is [[48]] (he).

In the 2016 World Table Tennis Championships, Ma won his [[49]] (two) world championship. Finally at 28, Ma got his Grand Slam (大满贯).

Ma once said, “It was the happiest moment of my life when I saw the national flag of the People’s Republic of China being raised because of me. I finally realized my dream of [[50]] (win) honors for my motherland—the dream since my childhood.”
answer: (1) players；(2) was；(3) Although/Though；(4) up；(5) himself；(6) second；(7) winning
explanation:
句意：马龙被广泛认为是乒乓球历史上最伟大的运动员之一。根据“Ma Long is widely regarded as one of the greatest...in the history of table tennis.”可知，one of the + 形容词最高级 + 名词复数，表示“最……之一”，play的名词形式表示“运动员”是player，这里要用复数形式players。故填players。

句意：他从小就喜欢打乒乓球。根据“He has been enjoying playing table tennis since he...a child.”可知，since引导的时间状语从句，从句用一般过去时，主语是he，be动词用was。故填was。

句意：尽管他失败了很多次，但他日复一日地坚持训练。根据“...he failed many times, he kept on training day after day.”可知，前后是转折关系，且空格在句首，用although或though表示“尽管”，首字母大写。故填Although/Though。

句意：他不想放弃他的梦想。根据“He didn’t want to give...his dream.”可知，give up表示“放弃”，是固定搭配。故填up。

句意：教练告诉他，唯一能打败他的人就是他自己。根据“the only one who can beat him is...(he).”可知，这里表示“他自己”，用反身代词himself。故填himself。

句意：在2016年世界乒乓球锦标赛上，马龙赢得了他的第二个世界冠军。根据“Ma won his...(two) world championship.”可知，这里表示“第二个”，用序数词second。故填second。

句意：我终于实现了为祖国赢得荣誉的梦想——这个自童年以来的梦想。根据“I finally realized my dream of...(win) honors for my motherland”可知，of是介词，后接动词的动名词形式，win的动名词是winning。故填winning。

subject: english
content:
根据下面的对话内容，在空白处填上一个适当的句子或短语，使对话的意思连贯、完整。

A: Hello, Fu Xing. Is that your new bicycle?

B: Yes. I’ve just bought it.

A: [[51]]?

B: It was made in Shanghai.

A: I also want to buy one. [[52]]?

B: I bought it on JD.com using the national shopping subsidy (国家购物补贴) to save some money.

A: The shopping subsidy? But I don’t know how to use it.

B: Don’t worry. I can help you.

A: [[53]].

B: It’s my pleasure. The bicycles are in different colors. [[54]]?

A: I like green best. [[55]]?

B: You can get the bicycle in about two days. JD Express will deliver it to you.

A: Great!
answer: (1) Where was it made?；(2) Where did you buy it?；(3) Thank you.；(4) Which color do you like?；(5) How soon can I get it?
explanation:
根据答语“It was made in Shanghai.”可知，它是在上海制造的，所以此处在询问自行车的产地。故填Where was it made?

根据答语“I bought it on JD.com using the national shopping subsidy (国家购物补贴) to save some money.”可知，此处询问对方是在哪里买的自行车。故填Where did you buy it?

根据答语“It’s my pleasure.”可知，此处表达感谢。故填Thank you.

根据答语“I like green best.”可知，此处询问对方喜欢什么颜色。故填Which color do you like?

根据答语“You can get the bicycle in about two days. JD Express will deliver it to you.”可知，此处询问多久能收到自行车。故填How soon can I get it?

subject: english
content:
时光悄然流转，成长的印记藏在每一次小小的改变里。请根据提示，结合自己的真实经历，以“How I’ve Changed!” 为题，写一篇英语短文。

要求：1. 至少80词；

2. 包含所提示要点，并适当进行拓展；

3. 文中不能出现真实姓名和所在学校名称。

How I’ve Changed!
answer:
How I’ve Changed!

Time flies. I’ve changed a lot.

In appearance, I was short and thin before, but now I’m taller and stronger. My hair was short, but now it’s long. In personality, I used to be shy and quiet. Now I’m outgoing and like making friends. For hobbies, I used to watch TV and play games. Now I like reading and playing basketball. The most important change is that I’m more independent. Last year, when my parents were away, I took care of myself. It made me grow up.

I like my changes. They make me better.

(2025·佛山高三调研)

In the age of the selfie, taking photos of yourself has become a daily activity. Half of all teenagers regularly post selfies. But what happens when the desire for the best selfie starts damaging nature—or even ourselves?

Social media tourism is dramatically changing people who visit natural places like Figure Eight Pools in Sydney’s Royal National Park. Many people are now drawn to these places for the best selfie background. These new tourists, motivated to seek out photos and selfies, sometimes ignore warning signs or bans on drones (无人机). Thus, many people have been severely injured or killed by taking risky selfies and photos in dangerous locations. Additionally, drone use can cause environmental harm if drones catch fire or batteries leak.

The search for the perfect selfie can also harm animals, protected plants and even First Nations rock art. In some cases, selfies have become a long-term threat to ecosystems.

But for land managers, perhaps the biggest challenge is satisfying increased interest while keeping people safe. They are working to assist this new demand by reshaping nature to make better scenery—and keep visitors safer. At Moran Falls in Queensland’s Lamington National Park, a famous view had been blocked by plants, driving some visitors to jump the fence at the viewing platform and stand directly on top of a very tall cliff (悬崖). As a solution, land managers have the trees trimmed (修剪) and then use the fallen branches to hide the track made by selfie-seekers.

These land managers are wondering why traditional measures like signs and warnings often prove ineffective. The answer may lie in social recognition.For many, the risk seems worth the reward if it means gaining admiration on social media. Nature-based content on popular social media platforms often perform very well, giving other would-be influencers the motive to seek out new locations. This problem has been created by the combination of social media and human psychology. To solve it, we might look at how these two factors interact. Responsible selfie and tourism campaigns on popular social media platforms could be a start.
content: Why are many people attracted to visit places like Figure Eight Pools?
options: To search for the ideal selfie setting.
To test the use of drones for photography.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据第二段“Social media tourism is...for the best selfie background.”可知,许多人被吸引到像“八字池”这样的地方是为了寻找理想的自拍环境。故选C。

subject: english
material:
(2025·莆田高三三模)

A humanoid robot can relay video and touch sensations to a person wearing a haptic (触觉的) feedback suit and a virtual reality (VR) headset hundreds of kilometres away, offering away for people to attend events without travelling.

The iCub 3 robot is a 52-kilogram, 125-centimetre-tall robot with 54 joints across its body. Its head contains two cameras where a human’s eyes would be, and an Internet-connected computer where the brain would go. Along with the cameras, sensors covering its body send data to the robot’s “brain”. These sensations are then reproduced on a suit and VR headset worn by a remote human operator.

When the operators react to what they see and feel, the suit’s sensors pick up the movements and the robot matches them. “The key is to translate every signal and bit of digital data that can be sent through the network.” says Stefano Dafarra, who was part of the iCub 3 team. There can be a small delay of up to 100 milliseconds to capture and transmit the visual shots, but the operator can case this by moving slightly slower than normal.

The team demonstrated the robot at the Venice Biennale, where it wandered through an exhibition while its operator stood 290 kilometres away in Genoa. Dafarra hopes people will use the iCub 3 to attend events remotely, reducing the need to travel. “But at present, a fall could be hugely damaging to the robot, and it’s uncertain whether it could stand up again on its own,” he says.

“iCub 3 is an interesting robot and offers clear advantages from the previous versions.” says Jonathan Aitken, whose laboratory owns a prior version of the robot. However, he is disappointed that the team wasn’t clear in its research about the data transmission requirements of the new version of the robot. “It would be good to know just how much data was required, and what the upper and lower bounds were.” he says.
content: What’s the principle behind the humanoid robot?
options: It conveys sensations to the wearer and acts accordingly.
It receives commands from an operator through the Internet.
The cameras take pictures and then interact with the sensors.
The computer in the robot processes the data and gives orders.
explanation: 细节理解题。文章第二段讲到“Along with the cameras, sensors...by a remote human operator.”可知,人形机器人背后的原理是它把感知传达给佩戴者并据此行动。故选A。

subject: english
material:
How to choose a hiking trail (路径)

If you’re a keen hiker,chances are that you have your favourite trails mostly because they’re easy to reach and fit into your schedule. If you desire to set foot in hiking in depth,this guide may walk you through the steps of how to choose a hiking trail to your next great adventure.

[[1]],defining how many miles the hike covers before departure. Next,ask yourself if you can reasonably walk that far. You can just walk as far down a trail as you want,and then turn back when you’re ready.[[2]],such as a waterfall or standing stones,you’ll ideally make sure you can reach it.

Know what’s going to be underfoot.[[3]].On a hike you might encounter all different types of land,and the climbing is going to be dangerous or stable. So do research and understand what type of terrain (地形) you’re likely to encounter. There’s a big difference between walking through a forest and stair-stepping up a steep rock. When you’re using route finding apps,trails are usually rated as easy,moderate or difficult. Make sure you understand exactly what the hike involves from a skill to equipment.[[4]]

For hikers,a thundering waterfall falling over a cliff can be a breathtaking climax to a forest hike.[[5]],the things you’ll see along the way are a great reason to choose one hiking trail over another—so long as the rest of it falls within your ability level of course.
options: Even if they are worth visiting
But if there’s a waymark you’re hoping to see
It helps you decide between hiking shoes or boots
Although not all hikes lead to a fantastic viewpoint
Don’t rush into the journey without the investigations above
explanation: 空后一句提到在出发前确定远足要走多少英里,以及自己能否走完这段距离。C项与距离相关。另外,C项中的“distance”与后文的“how many miles”相呼应。故选C项。

subject: english
content:
阅读材料并补全短文，每空一词。

Books are very important in our lives. Reading a good book helps us to learn and relax. Today, with the development of technology (随着科技发展), we have more ways to read. Audiobooks (有声读物) are one of them. Usually we read books word by word, but audiobooks give us a new way to “read”: we listen to books.

With the help of audiobooks, we can “read” anytime and anywhere. We can listen to a book when we are on the bus, doing housework, walking the dog, or just relaxing at home.

Also, listening to audiobooks can give our eyes a rest. Looking at books for a long time is bad for our eyes. With audiobooks, we can still enjoy the stories in audiobooks but without making our eyes tired.

At the same time, music and sound of audiobooks make the stories more enjoyable (有乐趣). What’s more, audiobooks can protect the environment (保护环境). They don’t need paper—that means we don’t have to cut down (砍伐) trees.

Now more and more people enjoy this new way of listening to books around the world. Do you want to try it?

Today, I read a passage about audiobooks. Audiobooks are a new kind of book. And now more and more people around the world enjoy [[62]] to books in this new way. Do you know why? [[63]], we can “read” books anytime and anywhere. Second, they are [[64]] for eyes. Third, they make stories more enjoyable with music and sound. Last, we don’t have to cut down [[65]] to make it.

subject: english
material:
阅读下列短文，从每题所给的A、B、C、D 四个选项中选出最佳选项。

A

Every month we interview someone about their experiences of living abroad. This month we are speaking to Brian, a British guy, who worked in Aspen, an up-market ski resort in the state of Colorado.

Brian, how did you get the job?

Well, I was working for an oil company in Galveston, Texas, when there was a fall in the industry and I lost my job. I didn’t know what to do and was about to go back to England when a friend phoned to say he needed someone to manage his bar in Aspen, Colorado. I happened to have nothing better to do, so I decided to go for it.

Could you describe a typical day for you in Aspen?

When I first got there, I tried to do as much skiing as possible. I’d get up fairly early, about 8:30, go down to get some breakfast, get all my gear on, and head out to the slopes. I’d come back about 1 p.m and get some lunch. I opened the bar around 3 p.m. But after a few weeks of that, I got pretty tired, so I did a lot less skiing.

What was the work like?

It was all fairly easy. I was in charge of about four other bartenders, and we worked till 12 midnight. After closing the bar, it took about an hour to get everything cleaned up. I usually got to bed about 1:30, unless I decided to go for a night out on the town.

What were the best things about working in Aspen?

Well, I loved the job. I got to meet loads of really interesting people and made lots of useful contacts. Also, the weather is great: blue skies and cold weather—which is great for skiing as the snow doesn’t melt too much in the afternoon. And because Aspen is so expensive, it never gets too crowded.
content: Why did Brian decide to work for the bar?
options: Because he wanted to stay in America.
Because he wanted to earn more money.
Because he lost his job in the oil company.
Because he had experience in managing bars.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据Brian, how did you get the job?部分的“Well, I was working for an oil company in Galveston, Texas, when there was a fall in the industry and I lost my job. I didn’t know what to do and was about to go back to England when a friend phoned to say he needed someone to manage his bar in Aspen, Colorado. I happened to have nothing better to do, so I decided to go for it.(嗯，我当时在得克萨斯州加尔维斯顿的一家石油公司工作，后来行业不景气，我失业了。我不知道该怎么办，正打算回英国时，一个朋友打电话来说，他需要有人来管理他在科罗拉多州阿斯彭的酒吧。我当时正好没什么别的事可做，所以就决定去试试。)”可知，布莱恩决定去那家酒吧工作是因为他在石油公司失业了。故选C。

subject: english
material:
Judith Allen was one historian whose sudden and untimely death in London has shocked and saddened many historians.

I first met Judith in 2006 when I was working at the Menzies Centre at King’s College London. Thrilled to have struck up a friendship with a scholar whose work had been extremely important to my History PhD, I was invited to her London flat for brunch. I was a little surprised to discover on arrival that this would not be an intimate occasion, but the crowd made sense when our hosts announced that this was not an ordinary brunch gathering but their wedding. It was a warm and happy celebration and there was a lot of laughter.

Some months later Judith was invited as a speaker at a conference on feminism (女权主义). Her lecture turned out to be a great success, showing people’s interest in her topic and her fame in Britain. Ours was a short and quick friendship in Judith’s richly connected and intellectually active life, but her generosity and insights have stuck with me.

When I returned to Australia, her ongoing companionship took the form of books, chapters and articles that have always been close to hand. When I had started my PhD in 1999, Allen’s writings were models of feminist history that made it seem possible to write my own history of the pregnant body. Her thoughts in feminist and belief in poststructuralist approaches (后结构主义方式) to historical research offered a path in charting the changing nature of the pregnant body in Australian medicine, law and feminism. As I later restarted my research after receiving my PhD, her historical interventions continued to inform and guide me.
content: What does the underlined part“an intimate occasion” in paragraph 2 refer to?
explanation: 词句猜测题。根据第二段中“I was a little surprised to discover on arrival that this would not be an intimate occasion, but the crowd made sense when our hosts announced that this was not an ordinary brunch gathering but their wedding.(我到达后有点惊讶地发现这并非an intimate occasion，不过当主人宣布这不是一场普通的早午餐聚会而是他们的婚礼时，现场的人群就显得合情合理了)”可知，“an intimate occasion”与后文出现的“the crowd(人群)”形成鲜明对比，指小型的私人聚会。故选B。

subject: english
material:
When David Howes thinks of his home city of Montreal, he thinks of the bells and the smell of food being cooked over wood fires. But when he stopped at his local tourism office to ask where they recommend that visitors go to smell, taste, and listen to the city, he just received blank stares. “It seems like they only knew about which things there were to see,” says Howes,the director of Concordia University’s Center for Sensory Studies.

Around the world, researchers like Howes are looking into how nonvisual information defines the character of a city and affects its livability. Oguz Oner, an academic and musician, has spent years organizing sound walks in Istanbul where blindfolded (蒙住眼睛的) participants describe what they hear at different places. His research has figured out locations where vegetation could be planted to reduce traffic noise or where a wave organ could be built to strengthen the comforting sounds of the sea.

Researchers use various ways to get people’s feelings towards the sensory experiences. But as data collection becomes more widespread, many experts warn the public about privacy. Fairness and inclusion also come into play when determining whose sensory experiences should be included into urban planning. Poor urban communities have typically suffered noise and odor pollution from highways and factories, yet they are also often targeted by noise complaints, for example, when their neighbourhoods gentrify (贵族化).

“Sensory perceptions are not neutral, or simply biological; whether we find something pleasant or not has been shaped culturally and socially,” says Monica Montserrat Degen, an urban cultural sociologist at Brunel University London. Degen uses the example of a London neighbourhood where cheap restaurants that served as hangouts for local youth were replaced by fashionable cafes. “It used to smell like fried chicken,” she says, but new comers found it annoying rather than welcoming. “Now it smells like cappuccinos.”
content: Why did Howes receive blank stares?
options: They didn’t know he was an expert.
They focused mainly on visual attractions.
They were not trained to answer his question.
explanation: 推理判断题。根据第一段“It seems like they only knew about which things there were to see(他们似乎只知道有哪些景点可看)”可知，Howes得到一脸茫然是因为那些人主要关注视觉景点。故选C。

subject: english
material:
Languages are like living organism, developing over time. Charles Darwin himself noted the similarities.“The formation of different languages and of distinct species,” he writes in The Descent of Man,“are parallel (平行的).”

Now, new research in Nature Ecology & Evolution shows that the similarity runs deeper.Islands, long recognized as drivers of biological diversity (多元化), are just as much engines of linguistic (语言学的) diversity. Drawing on a database of languages from more than 13,000inhabited (有人居住的) islands, the study shows that some of the same patterns hold true in both life and language.

In 1967, biologists proposed that the number of plant and animal species on any given island depends largely on two factors: its size and its distance from the mainland. The larger the island, the closer to continents, the more species it has. In line with the first principle, Lindell Bromham, leader of the study, and her colleagues found that the number of languages on an island increases with area. As for the second, they didn’t find a direct relationship. This is probably because, while plants and animals only come to islands by chance, humans do it on purpose.

Island languages tend to have far fewer phonemes (音位) than mainland ones. Perhaps these languages lose phonemic diversity in the same way that populations lose genetic diversity when they separate from the mainland. Another possibility is that in faraway populations, there are not many neighbouring languages to mix, so speakers don’t need as many. Yet another difference between island languages and species is that plants and animals are going extinct at a worrying speed, with 50 percent of endangered species living on islands. Languages are also in danger, but based on this new study, island languages are no more endangered than those on the mainland.

Nevertheless, Bromham says that protecting island languages is crucial.“We want to highlight how amazing it is that we have all these different solutions to human communication.Any language loss is a loss for all of us,” she says.
content: What does the new research show?
options: Darwin’s theory is supported by linguistic data.
Inhabited islands are home to different languages.
Languages and species develop at the same speed.
Islands drive both biological and linguistic diversity.
explanation: 细节理解题。根据第二段“Now, new research in Nature Ecology & Evolution shows that the similarity runs deeper. Islands, long recognized as drivers of biological diversity, are just as much engines of linguistic diversity.(现在，《自然生态与进化》杂志上的新研究表明，这种相似性更为深刻。长期以来，岛屿一直被认为是生物多样性的驱动力，而它们同样是语言多样性的引擎。)”可知，新的研究显示岛屿推动了生物和语言的多样性。故选D。

Languages are like living organism, developing over time. Charles Darwin himself noted the similarities.“The formation of different languages and of distinct species,” he writes in The Descent of Man,“are parallel (平行的).”

The larger the island, the closer to continents, the more species it has. In line with the first principle, Lindell Bromham, leader of the study, and her colleagues found that the number of languages on an island increases with area. As for the second, they didn’t find a direct relationship. This is probably because, while plants and animals only come to islands by chance, humans do it on purpose.

Island languages tend to have far fewer phonemes (音位) than mainland ones. Perhaps these languages lose phonemic diversity in the same way that populations lose genetic diversity when they separate from the mainland. Islands are the engines of language and life.

subject: english
material:
阅读下面短文，从短文后的选项中选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。选项中有两项为多余选项。

Baking is the process of cooking food by dry heat in an oven. It’s a culinary (烹饪的) art, transforming simple ingredients into creations that satisfy our tastes and nourish our bodies.[[16]].

Baking as mindfulness

Psychologists describe mindfulness as paying attention to the present moment. Baking does exactly that: the rhythm of stirring, the smell of vanilla and the soft feel of dough.[[17]]. Research shows that everyday creative activities like cooking and baking are linked with improved mood and lifted spirit.

Baking and neurodiverse minds

For neurodiverse people, baking can be a powerful experience. The structure of a recipe gives a sense of order, while the sensory parts can be deeply comforting. Repetitive actions help calm the nervous system and regulate focus.[[18]]. Following steps, managing time, and adjusting when something goes wrong strengthen planning and flexibility.

[[19]]

Of course, baking doesn’t always go smoothly. Sometimes the cake sinks or one forgets an ingredient or adds too much of something. When the cake sinks, one may feel angry and disappointed. After the frustration fades, most people choose to try again. Baking teaches patience and helps us see that progress often comes through imperfect attempts.

Baking as a way to connect

[[20]]. In the psychiatric (精神病学的) unit, sharing cookies become a small but meaningful ceremony. When someone bakes a cake for his co-workers or neighbor, the purpose is not to impress anyone; rather, it was an act of kindness. It is said that sharing food promotes belonging and connection, both of which are linked to emotional well-being.
options: They all keep one in the moment
It also brings people spiritual benefits
Baking becomes an increasingly popular lifestyle nowadays
The most rewarding aspect is that baking brings people together

It’s a culinary (烹饪的)art, transforming simple ingredients into creations that satisfy our tastes and nourish our bodies.(烘焙是将食物放入烤箱，通过干热进行烹制的过程。它是一门烹饪艺术，能把简单的食材转化为满足味蕾、滋养身体的美味之作。)”提及烘焙能滋养身体。而下文均围绕烘焙对人的心理、精神层面的积极作用展开。选项E“It also brings people spiritual benefits (它还能为人们带来精神层面的诸多益处。)”以“also”实现从“身体滋养”到“精神益处”的递进，起到总领下文的作用，完美衔接上下文逻辑。故选E。

subject: english
content:
阅读下面短文，在空白处填入1个适当的单词或括号内单词的正确形式。

The Louis Vuitton Beijing Espace Culturel Art Space is showcasing“Painting from Nature,”an exhibition featuring the works of famous artists Joan Mitchell and Megan Rooney. It offers [[36]] unique dialogue between two generations of abstract expressionism.

Mitchell, [[37]] passed away in 1992, was a key figure in the Abstract Expressionist movement. She was good at drawing inspiration [[38]] masters such as Monet, Van Gogh and Cézanne. Her famous works, [[39]] (affect) by the landscapes of Vétheuil along the Seine, use color and light to stir up deep emotional responses.

In contrast, Rooney, born in 1985 and based in London, [[40]] (know) for her dynamic, large-scale paintings [[41]] often includes performative elements in her creation. Her 2022exhibition, “The Fugue of Color” at the Louis Vuitton Foundation in Paris, was admired for its [[42]] (create) combination of artistic forms.

Running through Oct. 19, the event aims [[43]] (mark) the centennial (一百周年纪念) of Mitchell’s birth. And it will [[44]] (sure) serve as a bridge between her lasting legacy and Rooney’s modern innovation. It invites [[45]] (visitor) to engage with a sensory dialogue that connects past and present interpretations of abstract expressionism.
explanation:
考查冠词。句意：这场展览为两代抽象表现主义艺术家搭建起一场独特的对话。此处dialogue“对话”为可数名词，且此处泛指“一场对话”，故应用不定冠词，且unique的读音以辅音音素开头，故应用不定冠词a。故填a。

考查定语从句。句意：米切尔于1992年逝世，是抽象表现主义运动的核心人物。此处在句中引导非限制性定语从句，先行词为Mitchell，指人，在定语从句中作主语，故应用who引导。故填who。

考查介词。句意：她擅长从莫奈、梵高、塞尚等大师的作品中汲取灵感。此处意为“从……汲取灵感”，表达为draw inspiration from…，故应用介词from。故填from。

考查过去分词。句意：她著名的作品深受塞纳河畔韦特伊自然风光的影响，运用色彩与光线唤起观众深层次的情感共鸣。此处在句中作定语，修饰works，works与affect之间为被动关系，故应用过去分词作定语。故填affected。

考查主谓一致。句意：与之形成对比的是1985年出生于伦敦的鲁尼，她以充满动感的大幅画作闻名，并在创作中融入表演元素。此处在句中作谓语动词，主语为Rooney，为单数，与know之间为被动关系，且根据后文includes可知，此处陈述客观事实，故应用一般现在时。故填is known。

考查连词。句意：同上。此处is known for与includes为并列谓语动词，故此处应用连词and连接。故填and。

考查形容词。句意：其2022年在巴黎路易威登基金会展出的“色彩的赋格曲”因艺术形式的创造性融合而广受赞誉。此处修饰名词combination，故应用形容词“creative创造性的”作定语。故填creative。

考查不定式。句意：展览将持续至10月19日，旨在纪念米切尔诞辰一百周年。此处意为“旨在做某事”，表达为aim to do，故应用不定式作目的状语。故填to mark。

考查副词。句意：这场跨越时空的艺术对话必将成为连接米切尔永恒遗产与鲁尼当代创新的桥梁。此处修饰动词短语serve as，故应用副词“surely必然地，肯定地”作状语。故填surely。

考查名词的数。句意：邀请观众沉浸于一场贯通抽象表现主义过去与现在的感官对话。此处作宾语，故应用名词“visitor观众”，且此处指邀请很多观众，故应用名词的复数形式作宾语。故填visitors。

When Modern Technology Meets Intangible Cultural Heritage

Last Friday, our school organized a visit to the City Science Museum, where an exhibition themed “Modern Technology and Intangible Cultural Heritage” was held. More than 200 students took part in the activity, guided by our English teachers. The exhibition presented traditional crafts such as paper-cutting, shadow puppetry and sugar painting with the help of modern technologies. Through VR headsets, we experienced ancient workshops, while AI screens showed how masters create their works step by step. The most impressive part was the AR interaction—we “painted” virtual sugar art on tablets, with the effect vividly simulating real molten sugar. This activity bridged tradition and technology, deepening our love for intangible cultural heritage and inspiring us to protect it with innovation.

subject: english
content:
阅读下面短文，从方框中选择适当的词语填空。方框中有两个词语为多余选项。

A lot of people play sports，but very few people become sports professionals(专家)．If sports aren’t going to be your [[1]] job，why should you play them? Why should you train every day? Why should you work hard and make yourself feel sore(酸痛的) the next day? Wouldn’t it be better to forget sports and only pay attention to your [[2]]？

In fact，there are a lot of reasons to play sports.

First of all，sports are a great way to exercise.Doing exercise keeps you [[3]] and strong.It helps you stay in a good condition.When you exercise，your body makes endorphins(内啡肽) which give you more energy and make you feel [[4]].

Also，sports teach young people how to communicate and work as a team.They teach young people to respect their coaches(教练)，teammates and players from the other team.Many reports say that sports help young people stay [[5]] trouble.If a young person plays sports，he or she may have fewer problems.This is because sports teach people about rules.They also teach people that if they work hard，they might [[6]].

Another good way of sports is that they make people leave their houses.These days，a lot of people spend too much time watching television and playing video games.When you play sports，you go outside and exercise [[7]] the sun.You take in fresh air.All of these things are important.

Maybe you’re not going to become a sports professional，but that doesn’t matter.Sports will help you become a better and happier person.
explanation:
句意：如果体育不会成为你未来的工作，你为什么要进行体育运动呢？根据“If sports aren’t going to be your...job”和备选词可知，这里说体育不会成为未来从事的工作，future“未来的”，修饰名词“job”。故填future。

句意：难道忘掉体育，只关注你的学业不是更好吗？根据“Wouldn’t it be better to forget sports and only pay attention to your...”和备选词可知，与体育相对，这里说关注学业，study“学业，学习”。故填study。

句意：做运动让你保持健康和强壮。根据“Doing exercise keeps you...and strong.”和备选词可知，运动能让人保持健康，healthy“健康的”，keep healthy“保持健康”。故填healthy。

句意：当你运动时，你的身体会产生内啡肽，它会给你更多能量，让你感觉更快乐。根据“your body makes endorphins(内啡肽) which give you more energy and make you feel...”和备选词可知，内啡肽能让人心情愉悦，happier“更快乐的”符合语境。故填happier。

句意：很多报告称，体育运动有助于年轻人远离麻烦。根据“Many reports say that sports help young people stay...trouble.”和备选词可知，这里说远离麻烦，stay out of trouble“远离麻烦”。故填out of。

句意：它们还教导人们，如果努力，就可能成功。根据“They also teach people that if they work hard，they might...”和备选词可知，努力会带来成功，空格处需要动词作谓语，succeed“成功”，动词。故填succeed。

句意：当你进行体育运动时，你会走到户外，在阳光下锻炼。根据“When you play sports，you go outside and exercise...the sun.”和备选词可知，in the sun“在阳光下”。故填in。

subject: english

Skateboarding classes have found their way into schools! For sixth grader Carlos Cervantes，learning to skateboard takes a lot of work，but it pays off.“On the first day of class，I thought skateboarding would be scary.But I tried it，” said the 12-year-old boy.“After two days’ practice，I felt more comfortable.”

Carlos is learning to skateboard in an after-school program at West Middle School in Colorado.PE teachers start their skateboarding classes by teaching students how to put on their safety gear(装备)．Students then learn how to fall without getting hurt.And they start practicing.Sometimes they fall，but when they succeed，they smile heartily.

Skateboarding keeps kids active，benefits their health and develops new skills，also teaching them that persistence(坚持不懈) brings success.PE teacher Eric Klassen tells students not to say “I can’t” without hundreds of tries，and students follow this.

Many schools now offer “the new PE” like skateboarding，yoga and rock climbing—mostly individual sports.Schools launch these to fight childhood obesity，help students form lifelong fitness habits and give every student exercise chances，regardless of whether they join school sports teams.
content: What did Carlos Cervantes think of skateboarding on the first day of class? (no more than 6 words)
answer: He thought skateboarding/it would be scary.

content:
(2025·山东潍坊高二下期中)

The beautiful Li River is one of the most well-known tourist destinations in China’s Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.It attracts millions of visitors each year.However，its reputation as a top destination has had negative effects [[1]] the river’s water quality.

Previously，water quality in the Li River had suffered greatly from an increasing volume of tourists，many of [[2]] frequently threw garbage into the river.The growth in tourism also meant the local population rose [[3]](rapid)，as well as the number of commercial and industrial enterprises.In order to feed more people，more chemicals [[4]](use) to increase crop production.These chemicals led to severe water quality issues,[[5]](cause) an ongoing decrease in the number of fish species.Local officials were concerned that the pollution was damaging the natural environment [[6]] felt that urgent steps should be taken [[7]](restore) the river’s original beauty.

A comprehensive initiative was started，with a number of measures that [[8]](address) the issues.Dozens of polluting enterprises were closed or moved.The local government set up strict regulations regarding [[9]](far) industrial development.In addition，the local authorities began to use the media to spread environmental [[10]](aware) and encourage greater use of clean energy.With the measures，it is believed that the beauty of the Li River will be preserved for generations to come.
explanation:
考查介词。此处表示“对……产生负面影响”，应用固定短语have negative effects on/upon。故填on/upon。

考查定语从句。many of [[_]]frequently threw garbage into the river是非限制性定语从句，先行词是tourists，指人，关系词在从句中作介词of的宾语，应用关系代词whom引导。故填whom。

考查副词。空处修饰动词rose，应用副词rapidly作状语。故填rapidly。

考查动词时态、语态和主谓一致。空处作句子的谓语，句子描述过去发生的事情，应用一般过去时，且主语chemicals和动词use之间是被动关系，应用一般过去时的被动语态，主语是名词复数，be动词应用were。故填were used。

考查非谓语动词。空处作结果状语，主句与cause之间为主动关系，应用现在分词形式表示自然而然的结果。故填causing。

考查连词。“were concerned”和“felt”为并列谓语动词，应用连词and连接。故填and。

考查非谓语动词。空处作目的状语，应用动词不定式形式。故填to restore。

考查动词时态。空处作定语从句的谓语，句子描述过去发生的事情，应用一般过去时。故填addressed。

考查形容词比较级。此处表示“进一步的”，应用far的比较级further。故填further。

考查名词。空处作动词spread的宾语，应用名词awareness，意为“意识”，是不可数名词。故填awareness。

content:
(2025·山东临沂高二下期中)

This year’s World Earth Day theme is “Planet vs Plastics”．The day is [[1]] annual event that [[2]](honor) the achievements of the environmental movement and raises [[3]](aware) of protecting Earth’s natural resources for future generations.Aiming [[4]](create) a platform for governments，businesses，academic and social institutions to cooperate in dealing with the climate crisis，the first Shanghai Climate Week，[[5]] theme is “China Action，Asian Voice，Global Standard”，kicked off on April 22nd after months of preparations.

“China has made lots of efforts in carbon reduction.So we hope that through our actions，we can raise the voice of Asia and let the world see our efforts.[[6]] is also hoped that many of our actions and efforts will become standards for the future，” said Rao Wei，deputy secretary-general，Secretariat of Executive Committee，Shanghai Climate Week.

The Shanghai Climate Week also focused on the younger generation’s education and training in [[7]](sustain) development.“We also serve as a platform for international collaboration—[[8]](particular) emphasizing and enhancing knowledge exchange and practice-sharing.For example，we can bring the best practices in China to people and [[9]](country) around the world.And also，the other way round，” said Rao.“We will hold a series of activities and forums(论坛)，[[10]](discuss) paths to a greener world and helping China meet its carbon goals.”
explanation:
考查冠词。此处泛指“一个年度活动”，且annual的发育以元音音素开头，需用不定冠词an。故填an。

考查动词时态和主谓一致。that引导限制性定语从句，修饰先行词event，此处作并列谓语动词，句子陈述的是客观事实，时态应用一般现在时；event为单数，谓语动词应用第三人称单数形式。故填honors。

考查名词。此处作raises的宾语，应用名词形式awareness“意识”。故填awareness。

考查非谓语动词。aim to do sth为固定搭配，意为“旨在做某事”。故填to create。

考查定语从句。此处引导非限制性定语从句，先行词为the first Shanghai Climate Week，指物，关系词代替先行词在从句中作theme的定语，应用关系代词whose引导。故填whose。

考查形式主语。It is hoped that...为固定句型，此处为it作形式主语，真正的主语是that引导的主语从句，位于句首，首字母大写。故填It。

考查形容词。此处修饰名词development，应用形容词形式sustainable“可持续的”，作定语。故填sustainable。

考查副词。此处修饰动词emphasizing and enhancing，应用副词形式particularly“特别地”，作状语。故填particularly。

考查名词复数。country“国家”为可数名词，根据around the world可知，此处指不止一个国家，应用复数形式。故填countries。

考查非谓语动词。分析句子结构可知，此处应用非谓语动词，discuss“讨论”与逻辑主语We之间是主动关系，应用现在分词discussing，作状语。故填discussing。

It also has 51 types of mammals (哺乳动物)， 36 kinds of reptiles (爬行动物)， 6 types of fish， and more than 300 kinds of birds. [[3]] There are big ones like bighorn sheep， mountain lions， and mule deer.

The animals aren’t all small either.
There is a lot of water in Death Valley.
It gets little rain a year， so there isn’t much water.
Water is the biggest challenge for anything that lives in Death Valley.
